# Characterise restored-cache invalidation (hybrid-attention behaviour)

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 3.

## Target outcome

Quantified answer to the hypothesis risk in the parent: this build is Qwen3.x
hybrid attention + recurrent/SWA, and llama.cpp already invalidates its own
context checkpoints, so a restored snapshot may be rejected or only partially
usable. Produce a measured invalidation rate by *reuse shape*, plus the tokens
re-processed as a result.

## Minimal implementation

- `--mode invalidation` in the harness, driving four restore shapes per size:
  1. exact replay — same prompt, no extension (best case);
  2. one-turn extension — same prompt + a short follow-up user turn (the real
     session pattern);
  3. prefix drift — same prompt with a modified system-prompt head (should
     always miss, guards against over-crediting);
  4. cold control — no snapshot at all.
- Parse llama-server log markers between requests: `forcing full prompt
  re-processing`, `erased invalidated context checkpoint ... n_swa`,
  `restored context checkpoint`, and `n_past = ... slot.prompt.tokens.size()`.
  Attribute markers to an attempt by slot id + log offset captured immediately
  before and after each request.
- Report per shape: restore-OK rate, full-reprocessing rate, mean/median tokens
  re-processed, and the effective usable prefix (cached tokens on the first
  completion after restore).
- Emit `results/<label>/invalidation.json` + markdown table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Invalidation table for the four restore shapes at each prompt size, with
  n >= 3 per cell: restore-OK rate, full-reprocessing rate, tokens re-processed
  (median/p90), effective usable prefix fraction.
- Requirement from `AGENTS.md` respected: `forcing full prompt re-processing` is
  reported as *expected hybrid-arch behaviour with a cost*, never as a defect —
  the table quantifies the cost, and the doc says so explicitly.
- The prefix-drift control behaves as expected (near-zero usable prefix); if it
  does not, the recording/attribution method is reported as unproven and the
  numbers are marked non-authoritative rather than published as fact.
- The one-turn-extension shape is measured, because it is the shape that decides
  whether virtual slots help real sessions (which always extend context).
- Log-marker attribution method is documented so another operator can reproduce
  the counts from the raw logs.

## Constraints

- llama-server logs carry no timestamps — attribution must use log byte offsets
  captured around each request, per the caveat in
  `docs/slot-persistence-analysis-harness.md`.
- Read-only access to `/var/log/llama-proxy/`; no log rewriting.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `scripts/slot_persistence_harness.py` (log-parsing reference)
- `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py` (window-metric reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/invalidation.json` (new artifact)

# Measure memory and page-cache pressure for N=8 session snapshots

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 4.

## Target outcome

The resource cost of holding 8 session snapshots instead of 2: per-snapshot
footprint, bytes per token, aggregate on-disk and host page-cache growth at N=8,
and the system `MemAvailable` delta — with VRAM reported as non-available rather
than guessed, per the fidelity convention in
`docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`.

## Minimal implementation

- `--mode memory` in the harness: build N=8 distinct session prefixes, save all
  eight (bounded by free page cache), then measure:
  - on-disk size per snapshot and total (also reported by
    `du -sb` on the run's own directory);
  - `/proc/meminfo` `Cached` and `MemAvailable` before/after each save and after
    the full set, plus the page-cache residency of the snapshot files;
  - read-back bandwidth: sequential read of each snapshot to `/dev/null` (the
    proxy's restore path reads the whole file), giving MiB/s — the term that
    determines restore cost as snapshots grow.
- Derive bytes/token per size and extrapolate to N=8 for a realistic mix,
  stating the mix used.
- Record the ROCm VRAM reading and mark it explicitly non-available/ungraded
  (the known-degraded ~0.2 GB reading), instead of reporting a false number.
- Emit `results/<label>/memory.json` + markdown table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Per-size snapshot footprint and bytes/token, measured (not derived-only).
- N=8 aggregate footprint (sum of snapshot sizes) and observed `Cached` growth,
  with the delta between them explained (page cache vs. written-but-not-resident).
- `MemAvailable` delta across a full N=8 set, and the maximum resident footprint
  observed during the run.
- Read-back bandwidth (MiB/s) for snapshot files, which the verdict uses to
  extrapolate restore cost.
- VRAM is either measured credibly or explicitly reported as non-available with
  the reason; no estimated VRAM figure is presented as measured.
- The run cleans up the snapshots it created and reports the post-cleanup
  `MemAvailable` / `Cached` return-to-baseline.

## Constraints

- Must not fill the page cache to the point of harming live inference: the run
  is bounded by a `--max-write-mib` guard (default sized from current
  `MemAvailable`) and stops early, recording truncation.
- No `drop_caches` unless explicitly permitted by the operator; measure the
  natural page-cache behaviour instead.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/kv_memory_table.py` (per-token KV expectation reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/memory.json` (new artifact)
- `scripts/cleanup-slot-cache.sh`

# Harness-side virtual-slot prototype: 8 session slots over 2 physical slots

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Measurement 5 — the end-to-end contention
comparison. **Gated on OPEN QUESTION 2** (recorded on the parent): AC5 of the
spike asks for 8 virtual slots over 2 physical slots, but virtual slots do not
exist and must not be added to production. This child delivers the measurement
as a *harness-side prototype* unless the producer directs otherwise.

## Target outcome

A measured p50/p90 first-byte latency and throughput comparison between
(A) 2 logical sessions on 2 physical slots (today's baseline) and (B) 8 logical
sessions multiplexed onto 2 physical slots by swap-in/swap-out of KV snapshots,
using a synthetic 8-concurrent-session workload.

## Minimal implementation

- `proxy/benchmarks/virtual_slot_prototype.py` (or a `--mode virtual` in the
  harness): an 8-entry session table mapping logical session → physical
  llama-server slot; on dispatch it restores the session's snapshot into a free
  physical slot (evicting the current occupant with a save first), issues the
  completion, then saves the session's snapshot back.
- Workload: 8 concurrent synthetic sessions, each doing K turns with a shared
  prefix and per-turn growth, sized from the spike's four prompt sizes; turn
  gaps chosen to force real evictions.
- Metrics per configuration: TTFT p50/p90, per-session abandon count (requests
  that could not get a physical slot within the configured queue budget — the
  harness's analogue of `fallback_after_queue`), save/restore counts and
  failures, restored-hit rate, and completion count.
- Both configurations run back-to-back in one invocation so drift is shared.
- Emit `results/<label>/contention.json` + markdown table with an explicit
  A/B delta column.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A/B table for N_logical = 2 (baseline) vs N_logical = 8 over 2 physical slots:
  TTFT p50/p90, throughput, abandon count, save/restore counts, hit-rate,
  per-configuration duration.
- The eviction cost is counted, not hidden: for every restore that displaces
  another session, the displaced session's next-turn cold cost is measured and
  reported (this is the "eviction cost it imposes" term the parent requires).
- The run states plainly whether the prototype is a faithful model of a
  production virtual-slot implementation, listing the differences (no proxy
  routing, no dispatch leases, no contention queue) — no implied production
  parity.
- If 8-over-2 cannot complete within a bounded budget (e.g. wall-clock cap), the
  partial result is reported with the completion fraction rather than being
  silently truncated.
- The prototype lives only under `proxy/benchmarks/`; a test/documentation
  assertion confirms no production module is imported for dispatch.

## Constraints

- No production behaviour change (parent AC5).
- Must not starve live sessions: the run requires a quiet window or an explicit
  recorded validity caveat, mirroring
  `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` § `Fidelity caveats`.

## Risks

- Two prior live sweeps failed under concurrent load (600-760 s stalls,
  llama-server health probes unanswered). If the quiet window cannot be obtained,
  this child must fall back to the analytic model in the verdict child and say
  so — do not retry the live run indefinitely.

## Key Files

- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_save_restore_benchmark.py`
- `proxy/benchmarks/slot_benchmark.py` (concurrency/sweep reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_simulation.py` (queue-model reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/contention.json` (new artifact)

# Results doc: tables, break-even model, go/no-go verdict and substitutes

Parent: LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE. Satisfies AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC5 of the spike.

## Target outcome

A committed document `docs/virtual-slot-spike-LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE.md` containing
the complete measured tables, an explicit break-even inequality, a go/no-go
verdict, and — if not viable — the cheaper substitutes ranked with the measured
evidence for each.

## Minimal implementation

- Assemble the tables from the four measurement children's JSON artifacts
  (save size/time, restore time, restore hit-rate, invalidated-restore rate,
  memory delta, contention A/B). Cross-link each number to its result file and
  commit so the doc is auditable, not just descriptive.
- Break-even model, stated as an inequality with every term measured:
  `hit_rate × (cold_prefill_s − restore_s) > (1 − hit_rate) × eviction_reprefill_s + save_s_share`
  — or an equivalent explicit form — with the measured values substituted and
  the resulting break-even `hit_rate*` solved for each prompt size. State the
  cold-prefill baseline used (window median 61.8 s dispatch-first-byte, p90
  269.8 s) and the solitary cold-prefill figures from the parent's impact
  analysis (~254 new tok/s).
- Verdict: `go` (build virtual slots) / `no-go` (not viable) / `conditional`
  (viable only under a named condition), each with the driving measurement
  quoted. If `no-go`, rank the substitutes with measured evidence:
  more physical slots (LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8 — keep N=2 pending
  LP-0MVGPEP3O000RKKD), idle-aware admission (LP-0MVGD9Z8Z0055Y5J implementation
  done; LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD / LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF measurement), shorter
  post-stream lease (locate and cite the owning item).
- Fidelity section reproducing the caveat conventions
  (`docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md`): what could not be measured,
  VRAM non-availability, and the live-load validity caveat if applicable.
- AC5 proof: a `No production behaviour change` section listing the commits
  touched (`git diff --stat` restricted to `proxy/benchmarks/`, `proxy/tests/`,
  `docs/`), confirming `proxy/config.yaml` sha unchanged and proxy healthy after
  the runs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/virtual-slot-spike-LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE.md` committed with all six
  required tables: save size/time, restore time, restore hit-rate,
  invalidated-restore rate, memory delta, end-to-end contention metrics.
- The break-even condition is an explicit inequality with measured terms
  substituted, and the break-even hit-rate is solved per prompt size.
- Verdict is one of `go` / `no-go` / `conditional`, with the decisive measurement
  quoted and linked to its result artifact.
- If `no-go` or `conditional`, at least three cheaper substitutes are named with
  the measured evidence for each (or, where a substitute is unmeasured, that is
  stated as an open measurement with the owning work-item id).
- A fidelity/caveats section states every non-measured quantity explicitly, with
  no estimated value presented as measured.
- AC5 is evidenced: the diff touches only benchmark/test/doc paths, config sha
  unchanged, proxy verified healthy after the runs.
- Every number in the doc traces to a committed result file.

## Constraints

- Read-only on production configuration. No items in `proxy/proxy/` modified.
- The doc must not re-derive historical baselines it can cite (61.8 s median,
  269.8 s p90 from the parent's window).

## Key Files

- `docs/virtual-slot-spike-LP-0MVGD9ZKI004ETTE.md` (new)
- `docs/slot-count-verdict-lp-0mv9ungeb009xuz5.md` (format/caveat reference)
- `docs/slot-count-reevaluation-LP-0MVGCQ3QN009HRE8.md` (validity-caveat reference)
- `proxy/benchmarks/results/<label>/*.json`

## Goal (user story)

As an operator of the LLM proxy, I want the 24-hour usage report to include a
"local-turn coverage" section so I can see which sessions actually used the
local LLM, how many turns it answered, what share of the session's turns were
local, and why each session moved to remote — so I can judge whether local is
under-utilised and why.

## Context

The delivered analysis (24h window 2026-10-23 10:52 → 2026-10-24 10:52)
showed that 26 of 175 sessions had at least one turn routed to local, and all
225 such turns were answered (100% completion: 214 tool_calls, 10 stop,
1 length). 149 sessions never used local. A proposed section renders this as
three deterministic tables:

1. **Summary table** — rows P10 / P50 / P90 (+ totals) over the sessions with
   ≥1 local turn, columns: # turns local, # turns remote, % local turns,
   context size at fallback. Sorted by # turns local ascending in the
   percentile rows, more local turns being the goal. Session ID and fallback
   reason are categorical and therefore excluded from the percentile table;
   the reason distribution is provided as its own counts-and-% table (2).
2. **Fallback-reason summary table** — one row per fallback reason with a
   count and a % of the sessions-with-local (P50 # turns local 4.5, # turns
   remote 14.5, % local turns 26.2%; reference-window reason tally below).
3. **Per-session sampling table** — every session with ≥1 local turn,
   columns: session ID, # turns local, # turns remote, % local turns, reason
   for remote fallback, context size at fallback; sorted by # turns local
   descending (more local = better, best first). 26 rows in the reference
   window. % local turns = local / (local + remote) × 100 per session.

Operational definitions:

- "Routed to local for at least 1 turn and receives a response": a local
  `Stream started` (provider=local) paired with a local `Stream finished`
  (provider=local). All 225 routed turns were answered in the reference
  window; a routed-but-errored turn (Stream finished reason=error) would be
  counted as routed but flagged as unanswered rather than dropped.
- "% local turns": per-session share of turns answered by local
  (local / (local + remote), null when a session has no remote turns →
  100%). Percentiles of this column use linear interpolation like the others.
- "Context size at fallback": `estimated_tokens` from the session's
  `routing_skip_local` line at/near its recorded fallback (remote_move_time),
  falling back to the first remote stream's prompt tokens, and finally to
  start_context_size/max_context_size from the session CSV. Sessions whose
  log lines carry no `tokens=` value render an explicit n/a (3 of 26 in the
  reference window: empty_response / fallback_after_queue sessions) — never a
  fabricated estimate.
- Fallback reason: the session's existing attributed fallback_reason,
  sourced from the session's OWN evidence only (current report contract,
  LP-0MVMBMSWR0036RES): own routing_skip_local first, else own
  routing_skip_provider_context, else own Fallback triggered, else — only
  for rotated logs predating the session stamp — the nearest session-less
  fallback line within 60s. Explicit states: `no_remote_fallback`,
  `lease_denied` (local_lease_active refusal), `unattributed` (no own
  evidence). A session's reason is never inherited from an unrelated
  neighbour's global fallback line.

Reference-window fallback-reason tally (26 sessions): rate_limited 11
(42.3%), no remote fallback 4 (15.4%), empty_response 3 (11.5%),
provider_context_exceeded 2 (7.7%), local_concurrency_limit 2 (7.7%), and one
each (3.8%) of HTTP 503, fallback_after_queue, large_context_bypass,
context_too_large.

Notable findings the section should surface as interpretation notes:

- Context-size fallbacks never occur on a session's first message (median
  first-message prompt ~29.6K tokens vs cold_threshold 38000 / warm_threshold
  120000); they fire only after context grows past the thresholds. Reference
  window: 0 of 5268 local-to-remote fallbacks were first-message.
- 96.6% of local-to-remote fallbacks happen before the session has produced
  any local work (routing is decision-first, so local is declined
  pre-emptively, not after a failed attempt).
- rate_limited is the proxy's own per-provider RPM budget pacing
  (provider_budget.py BudgetDecision reason=rate_limited: the configured
  rate_limit_rpm window for that provider entry is exhausted and the request
  is passed through to the next provider immediately), NOT an upstream HTTP
  429 — those surface as upstream_http_error status=429 events instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: report.md contains a deterministic "Local model usage by session"
  section with the summary percentile table (P10/P50/P90 + total row over
  sessions with ≥1 local turn in the window) using the column set: # turns
  local, # turns remote, % local turns, context size at fallback.
- AC2: The section contains the fallback-reason counts-and-% summary table
  (reason, count, % of sessions-with-local).
- AC3: The section contains a per-session table listing each session with ≥1
  local turn: session ID, # turns local, # turns remote, % local turns,
  reason for remote fallback, context size at fallback; sorted by # turns
  local descending.
- AC4: Context size at fallback derives from routing_skip_local
  estimated_tokens at/near the session's fallback (falling back to the first
  remote stream's prompt tokens, then session CSV context columns); sessions
  without any token data render "n/a" with a limitation note, never a
  fabricated estimate.
- AC5: The section renders from the existing log/config inputs only (no new
  data sources); the per-session data is present in the session CSVs or an
  explicitly documented new artifact.
- AC6: Rule-based tests cover: session selection (≥1 local turn answered),
  percentile computation (P10/P50/P90, linear interpolation), % local turns
  derivation, fallback attribution (reason + context at fallback), the
  fallback-reason counts-and-% table, sort order, and the no-tokens n/a
  limitation path.
- AC7: The full suite passes via the test skill; the daily 05:00 cron run
  includes the new section with no agent in the loop.

## References

- Reference numbers (window 2026-10-23 10:52 → 2026-10-24 10:52): 26/175
  sessions with ≥1 local turn; 225 local turns, 225 answered; P50 local
  turns 4.5, P50 remote turns 14.5, P50 % local turns 26.2%, P50 context at
  fallback ~11K tokens; totals 225 local / 663 remote turns (25.3% local
  overall).
- Skill: .pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis (SKILL.md, REFERENCE.md, scripts/).


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25T03:2xZ (plan skill; session herdr-1792897925-2552737-30168):
  pre-check returned `skip` (effort Extra Small, risk Low) — auto-plan path:
  six-stage review only; no child items created.
- Corrected the fallback-reason operational definition to the implemented
  attribution contract (LP-0MVMBMSWR0036RES, completed): the prior wording
  ("own routing_skip_first, else nearest Fallback triggered within 60s")
  described the pre-fix attribution that inherited an unrelated neighbour's
  line (11/26 local-using sessions mislabelled as rate_limited in the
  reference window) and contradicted the analysis comment on this item.
- OPEN QUESTION (for implementer / producer): the description's
  reference-window numbers — 26/175 sessions, the fallback-reason tally
  (rate_limited 11, 42.3%; no remote fallback 4, 15.4%; etc.) and the P50
  context-at-fallback figure (~11K tokens) — were computed under the
  pre-fix nearest-line attribution. Recompute the reference numbers from
  real logs under the current attribution contract before finalising the
  section; treat the description's tally as indicative, not authoritative,
  when validating the new section's output.
data.title: Add local-turn coverage report to proxy usage analysis skill

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy maintainer, I want the unused `github` model chain (and its
`github-primary` provider entry) removed from `proxy/config.yaml`, so the
configuration reflects reality and carries no dead routing surface that could
silently attract traffic or confuse future readers.

## Evidence that it is unused

- `proxy/config.yaml` lines ~346-352 declare a `models.github` chain with a
  single remote provider `github-primary` (endpoint
  `https://models.inference.ai.azure.com`, aliases `github-*`).
- Zero traffic in every available proxy log (2026-10-17 14:46 → 2026-10-24
  10:35): no `provider=GitHub`, no `entry=github`, no `github-primary`, no
  `models.inference.ai` occurrences.
- In the 24h usage window (2026-10-23 10:52 → 2026-10-24 10:52) only three
  initial providers appear across 175 sessions: OpenCode, MunitoAI, and
  local/Qwen3.
- No test in tests/ or proxy/tests/ references the github chain.
- The only other reference is documentation: docs/routing.md:297 notes
  `github-primary` is deliberately ungated (no `model` declared). That note
  must be removed/updated with the chain.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The `github` chain (provider entry `github-primary` and its
  `github-*` aliases) is removed from proxy/config.yaml; no other chain
  references it.
- AC2: The resulting config loads cleanly — proxy startup/config-load tests
  pass, and a config validation/merge test confirms no dangling alias or
  provider reference remains.
- AC3: Documentation is consistent: docs/routing.md no longer describes
  `github-primary` as an ungated provider (remove the paragraph or restate it
  for a surviving ungated entry), and any config header comment naming it is
  updated.
- AC4: A regression test asserts the `github` chain is absent (config-load
  test), so the dead entry cannot be reintroduced unnoticed.
- AC5: If any client is found to request a `github-*` model alias (grep of
  shipped client configs), that must be reported and resolved before removal
  — otherwise AC1/AC4 stand.
- AC6: Full suite passes via the test skill before the change is closed.

## Notes

- The upstream model is unreachable anyway: `github-primary` declares no
  `model`, so the client chooses it; nothing in this deployment exercises
  that path. Removal also drops the "deliberately NOT gated" special case in
  the max_context_tokens documentation block (config.yaml ~line 324).
- Related: model chains shipped after removal are `embed`, `private`, `plan`,
  `author`, `code`, `compact`.

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer and analyst, I want a single per-turn correlation identifier
carried on every structured log line, so a request's full lifecycle — local
routing decision, fallbacks, stream start, stream finish, tokens — can be
reconstructed exactly instead of by FIFO pairing and nearest-line heuristics.

## Why

Today a turn leaves a trail of lines tied together only by session UUID and
timestamp ordering: `routing_skip_local` -> `Fallback triggered` xN ->
`Stream started` -> `Stream finished`. The analysis skill compensates with
heuristics (FIFO stream pairing, 60s fallback windows, nearest-attribution)
that mis-assign reasons (see the rate_limited misattribution in the
2026-10-23/24 window, where a session's own lease denials were overwritten by
an unrelated session's fallback line). A per-request id would remove every
one of these heuristics.

## Design note (plan in implementation)

Emitting an id at the earliest point a request is known (accept/entry) and
carrying it on: `routing_skip_local`, `routing_skip_provider_context`,
`Fallback triggered`, `routing_hop`, `local_dispatch_denied`, `[local]/[remote]
POST`, `Stream started`, `Stream finished`, `dispatch_first_byte_ms=`,
`ttft_seconds=`, and the error lines. Short (e.g. 8-hex) to keep lines
readable; both local and remote paths are in different modules
(`proxy/provider.py`, `proxy/router.py`, `proxy/proxy_remote.py`), so this is
a cross-cutting change with a shared helper.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A shared helper (e.g. in `proxy/utils.py` or a new module) generates
  and stamps a per-turn id, and the id is carried on all structured line
  kinds listed above (verify each emit site; no line kind may be left with
  the id unconditionally absent).
- AC2: The id is stable across the full lifecycle of one client request —
  including across fallback hops and chain-hold re-emissions — and unique per
  turn of a session (at minimum within the session).
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill consumes the id:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` parses it onto the
  relevant events; `aggregation.py` pairs streams, fallbacks, skips and TTFT
  events by id (falling back to today's heuristics only when the id is
  absent in older logs); `reporting.py` documents that per-turn attribution is
  exact where ids exist.
- AC4: Skill tests: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` lines with ids; new tests prove
  exact pairing by id (fallback -> stream, skip -> stream, TTFT -> stream)
  and that legacy lines without ids still parse via the existing fallback
  paths.
- AC5: Proxy tests asserting log text are updated where they instantiate or
  assert these lines: `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_model_audit_plan_routing.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_profile.py`.
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`,
  `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `scripts/analyse_slot_ratio_restore.py`,
  `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/correlate_oversized_sessions.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`; the pass-through log tail in
  `proxy/proxy/ui.py` is verified unaffected.
- AC7: Documentation: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` documents the id field and the
  exact-attribution semantics; SKILL.md notes no behavioural change.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill; no regression in the deterministic
  daily report path.

## Notes

- This supersedes most of the pairing heuristics in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis`; the change is cross-cutting, so split
  into sub-tasks during planning (shared helper + emit sites; parsers; skill
  consumption; tests) if useful.
- Backwards compatibility mandatory: old logs without ids must keep parsing.


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25: Pre-check returned `skip` (Extra Small, Low risk). Ran six automated review stages. Corrected AC4 `tests/fixtures.py` → `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`, AC7 `REFERENCE.md` → `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`. Plan complete — item ready for implementation.
data.title: Add per-turn correlation id to all structured log lines

## Goal (user story)

As the proxy-usage analyst, I want `Stream finished` lines to say explicitly
when an upstream reported no token usage, so "no data" is distinguishable from
"zero tokens" and sessions with unknown context are countable rather than
invisible.

## Why

`proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` only appends `tokens=prompt/completion/total`
when the upstream response carries a `usage` object:

```
if isinstance(usage, dict): ... parts.append(f"tokens=...")
```

When a provider (or an aborted/errored stream) omits usage, the line silently
has no `tokens=` field. In the 2026-10-23/24 window this left 3 of the 26
local-using sessions with no context size at all (their `Stream finished`
lines carry no tokens), so any analysis of "context at fallback" for them
degrades to n/a with no way to tell why at the log level.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When a terminal stream has no reportable usage, the `Stream finished`
  line carries an explicit marker (e.g. `tokens=missing` or `usage=none`),
  emitted from the same code path in `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`.
- AC2: The marker never overrides real usage — a present `usage` object still
  logs `tokens=p/c/t` exactly as today (no format change for the populated
  case).
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill counts the new marker:
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` parses it onto the
  stream-finished event, and `aggregation.py`/`reporting.py` report a
  "streams without usage" count (window-level, and per-session where the
  context-at-fallback table is rendered) instead of silently emitting n/a.
- AC4: `reporting.py` limitation text in the affected sections names the
  marker as the cause of missing context figures.
- AC5: Tests: a fixture line with `tokens=missing` in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`, plus tests in
  `test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` proving (a) missing-usage streams are counted
  and excluded from token totals, and (b) populated lines are unchanged.
  Proxy-side test for the emit path in `proxy/tests/` (whichever suite covers
  `router_helpers` stream-finish logging).
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated: `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`,
  `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` (any code doing
  `tokens=` regex matches must not treat `missing` as a number).
- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents the marker and its meaning.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — emit path for the `tokens=missing` marker (AC1, AC2, AC5).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` — parses the marker onto the stream-finished event (AC3).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/aggregation.py` — "streams without usage" count (AC3).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` — count in report + limitation text (AC3, AC4).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py` — fixture line with `tokens=missing` (AC5).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py` — analyser tests for the marker (AC5).
- `proxy/tests/test_stream_entry_name_logging.py` — proxy-side tests for the emit path (AC5).
- `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py` — consumer audit: `tokens=` regex must not treat `missing` as a number (AC6).
- `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py` — consumer audit (AC6).
- `proxy/scripts/analyze_context_distribution.py` — consumer audit (AC6).
- `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py` — consumer audit (AC6).
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md` — documents the marker and its meaning (AC7).

## Notes

- Small, contained change; the risk is consumers that regex
  `tokens=(\d+)/(\d+)/(\d+)` — those simply won't match the marker, which is
  the desired behaviour, but each should be verified rather than assumed.
data.title: Emit explicit tokens=missing marker when upstream reports no usage

## Goal (user story)

As a maintainer, I want the proxy's own request-budget skip to use a name that
cannot be confused with an upstream rate-limit rejection, so operators and
analysis tooling stop misreading `rate_limited` as "the local model was rate
limited".

## Why

`rate_limited` is emitted by `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py` when a provider
entry's configured `rate_limit_rpm` window is exhausted
(`BudgetDecision(reason="rate_limited")`). It is a **proxy-side, pre-flight
budget skip**, not an HTTP 429 from the provider — upstream 429s are logged
separately as `[remote] upstream error status=429` /
`upstream_http_error`.

The name caused a concrete misreading: `rate_limited` is 61.6% of the
fallback-reason table (6,042 events, all `from=munitoai-free`), yet it was
reported as the per-session "reason for remote fallback" for 11 of 26
sessions that had actually been diverted from local by lease contention. The
local provider has no `rate_limit_rpm` and can never emit this reason (0 of
9,683 archive occurrences are `from=local`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The budget-skip vocabulary is renamed to
  `provider_budget_exhausted`, everywhere it is emitted: the
  `BudgetDecision.reason` values in `proxy/proxy/provider_budget.py`
  (retaining the `_after_wait` / `_waiters` / `_disconnect` variants, e.g.
  `provider_budget_exhausted_after_wait`), the `reason=` text in the
  `Provider budget exhausted: skipping provider=...` log lines, the
  `fallback_reason = ...` assignments in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`
  (~9028, ~10515), **and the diagnostics attempt `status` values**
  `status="rate_limited"` / `status="rate_limited_waited"` (~9018, ~9038,
  ~10505, ~10525) -> `status="provider_budget_exhausted"` /
  `status="provider_budget_exhausted_waited"`. Producer decision
  (2026-10-25): *full rename everywhere* — no `rate_limited*` literal may
  remain in **newly emitted** code paths, tests, or current documentation.
  The analysis-skill legacy mapping (AC3) and `REFERENCE.md` deliberately
  retain the old spelling as a *historical* name (exactly as
  `warm_cache_bypass` is retained next to `context_too_large`).
- AC2: Internal decisions/behaviour are unchanged: the affinity/reserve/wait
  logic and any cooldown behaviour keep working (the rename must not alter
  decisions — it is a string rename only). `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES` is updated
  to key on the new status (`frozenset({"provider_budget_exhausted"})`,
  provider.py ~4181); `status_code=429` in the diagnostic attempt entries
  stays as-is (a numeric HTTP code, not the reason vocabulary); the
  reason-keyed budget-evidence gate `(reason or "").startswith("rate_limited")`
  (~669) switches to the new prefix.
- AC3: The usage-analysis skill normalises legacy logs: `log_parser.py` maps
  `rate_limited*` -> `provider_budget_exhausted*` so historical windows and
  new windows report under one label, with the mapping documented in
  `REFERENCE.md` (add to the existing legacy reason mapping next to
  `warm_cache_bypass` -> `context_too_large`).
- AC4: `reporting.py` renders the new label and keeps the reason table stable
  (no duplicate rows for old/new names in one window);
  `recommendations.py` text that references rate limiting is updated to
  distinguish proxy budget pacing from upstream 429s. Paths verified at plan
  time: `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/reporting.py` (legend at
  ~line 545) and `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/recommendations.py`
  (~lines 478, 544, 731).
- AC5: Tests: parser normalisation tests (old and new spellings) in
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/`; every test that asserts the old
  reason string is updated. Audited set (verified at plan time by literal
  scan): `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` (20 occurrences — the primary
  decision-reason tests), `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_munitoai_budget_eval_parse.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_quota_surge_bypass.py`, `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py`,
  `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/test_analyze_proxy_usage.py`,
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/tests/fixtures.py`,
  `tests/test_idle_admit_impact.py`.
  `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` and
  `proxy/tests/test_model_audit_plan_routing.py` were named in the original
  draft but contain **no** `rate_limited` literal — confirmed listed in error
  (producer decision 2026-10-25), nothing to change there.
  With the full rename the attempt-`status` assertions also move:
  `proxy/tests/test_provider_budget.py` (~1187), `proxy/tests/test_chain_hold_budget_window.py`
  (~75, ~169, ~397), `proxy/tests/test_quota_surge_bypass.py` (~357),
  `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py` (~360). Test-function names describing the
  old vocabulary are renamed in the same change (see implementation notes).
- AC6: Other log consumers audited/updated:
  `scripts/idle_admit_impact.py`, `scripts/slot-persistence-correlate.py`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/munitoai_budget_eval.py`,
  `proxy/benchmarks/contention_queue_profile.py`,
  `.worklog/analysis/extract_metrics.py`. Historical artifacts are
  deliberately left untouched: `.worklog/analysis/report.md` (regenerated by
  the analysis skill, which normalises legacy names via AC3) and
  `proxy/benchmarks/results/slot_sweep_2_3_4_20261023/RESULTS_NOTE.md`
  (archival run note quoting a then-current log line) — record this
  classification in the commit message.
- AC7: `REFERENCE.md` documents the vocabulary split (proxy budget skip vs
  upstream HTTP 429) so the two are never conflated again.
- AC8: Full suite passes via the test skill.
- AC9: Current documentation examples that show the reason *or* attempt-status
  strings are updated (`proxy/README.md` exhaustion-diagnostics example at
  ~lines 534-536 and table ~934, `proxy/docs/routing.md` routing table at
  ~lines 154-158, `proxy/MODEL_ADD.md` attempt example at ~lines 284-285) so
  no current doc advertises `reason=rate_limited` or `status: "rate_limited"`
  after the rename. `docs/dev/quota-surge.md` (~275) and
  `proxy/tests/test_quota_config_docs.py` (~44) cite the renamed test
  function `test_rate_limited_entry_still_skipped_under_surge` and are
  updated in lock-step with it.

## Notes

- **Deferral cleared:** renaming alone does not fix mis-attribution, it only
  removes a misleading label — so this was deferred behind the
  session-attribution fixes. The prerequisite LP-0MVMBMSWR0036RES (*Add
  session + attempt + budget evidence to `Fallback triggered` log lines*) is
  now `completed`/`in_review`, so the report is correct regardless of naming
  and this rename is unblocked.
- **Scope decided (producer, 2026-10-25): full rename everywhere.** The
  rename covers the budget-skip *reason* values **and** the diagnostics
  attempt *status* values, plus `_BUDGET_SKIP_STATUSES`, test assertions,
  fixtures, test-function names and documentation examples. **Boundary:** the
  rename targets the proxy budget-skip vocabulary only. It does **not**

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a measured comparison of **1 llama-server slot with
262,144 ctx** versus **2 slots with 131,072 ctx each**, so we can choose the
geometry that maximises local work served without unacceptable queueing.

## GATING PRECONDITION — do not start before this is met

**This experiment can only be carried out when we have a full night of GPU use
(>60% busy).** With local currently at ~10% busy, a 1-vs-2 slot comparison
measures noise, not saturation: the trade-off only shows up when demand
actually contends for slots. Verify the gate with the
`proxy-usage-analysis` report's `## Local model utilization` section for a
complete night window: busy must be >= 60% for the full night. Record that
evidence in a comment on this item before starting; if the gate is not met,
leave the item blocked.

## Why (current evidence, for context once the gate is met)

- Current geometry: `--parallel 2` with `--ctx-size 262144` = **131,072 tokens
  per slot**.
- Measured concurrency: **avg 1.04 while busy, peak 2** — demand is nearly
  serial today, so 2 slots are rarely both used.
- The routing hard cap (`local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold: 120000`)
  sits just under the 131K per-slot limit. In the 24h window **2,064 requests
  were skipped as `context_too_large`** (estimated > 120K), including 105
  skips from sessions that were already warm (cache ratio 0.92-1.00, only ~4K
  new tokens, total 126K-137K). A single 262K slot would move that ceiling
  from ~120K to ~258K.
- Local was idle **89.8%** of the window, serving only 225 turns across 26
  sessions, so spare capacity is not the current constraint — but slot
  geometry determines what will be servable once demand is raised.

## Hypothesis to test

- **1 x 262K**: ~2x per-slot context → far fewer `context_too_large` skips and
  larger conversations stay local; cost: requests serialise when two sessions
  overlap (today: peak 2, avg 1.04, so the cost may be small).
- **2 x 131K**: current state; parallel but capped at ~120K per request; the
  evidence above shows warm sessions being cut off at the cap.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC0 (GATE): A comment records the measured >60% GPU busy for a full night
  from the usage-analysis report, before any configuration change.
- AC1: A repeatable measurement protocol is defined and written on this item:
  identical workload window length, same metrics, same report tooling for both
  arms.
- AC2: Arm A (2 x 131K, current) and Arm B (1 x 262K) are each run for a
  comparable period at the gate, with llama-server `--parallel` / `--ctx-size`
  changed together (and `session_slot_pool_size` plus the warm/cold thresholds
  adjusted consistently, since per-slot ctx and slot count interact — see
  LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 / LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP on the band collapsing to zero
  width).
- AC3: Results compare, for each arm: local busy %, turns served locally,
  requests diverted per fallback reason (especially `context_too_large` and
  `large_context_bypass`), queue wait / `fallback_after_queue` counts, time to
  first token, prefill and decode phase slot-seconds, and any errors
  (`slot_save failed`, HTTP 400/503).
- AC4: A decision is recorded on this item: keep 2 slots, move to 1 slot, or
  make it mode-dependent, with the data that justifies it. If 1 slot wins, the
  follow-on config change is filed (or implemented if in scope).
- AC5: Findings feed the configuration documentation (`models.ini` launch
  flags, `proxy/config.yaml` slot/ctx comments) and the usage-analysis skill's
  interpretation section if the guidance changes
  (`.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/REFERENCE.md`), plus any log-consuming
  script that assumes a fixed slot count or per-slot ctx.
- AC6: Full suite passes via the test skill for any config/code change made.

## Notes

- Depends on demand having been raised first (thresholds / serve-first
  admission); that is why the >60% busy gate exists.
- Related: LP-0MSAOQTJS000FFVM (local ctx-size evaluation), and the
  prefill-latency optimisation item — decide geometry before micro-tuning.


---

## Plan (2026-10-25, /skill:plan)

Sequenced features in dependency order (execution order for `wl next`):

1. **Gate: verify 60% local busy night** (LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG) — parent AC0 evidence; blocks the arms.
2. **Geometry A/B protocol and reporter** (LP-0MVNCMDW50043RSP) — `docs/dev/slot-geometry-ab.md` (protocol, window, metrics, pre-registered gate), `scripts/slot_geometry_ab_report.py` + fixture tests, `scripts/slot_geometry_arm.py` apply/verify helper. Test-first; can start while the gate is unmet.
3. **Arm A capture: 2 slots 131K** (LP-0MVNCME7Y009KC9K) — blocked by 1+2.
4. **Arm B run: 1 slot 262K** (LP-0MVNCMEJ6004A2QY) — blocked by 3; warm ceiling raised to the 258,048 clamp, cold unchanged, band non-collapsed.
5. **Arm comparison and geometry decision** (LP-0MVNCMEV1007R6YY) — blocked by 4; applies the pre-registered gate, records verdict + follow-on item.
6. **Propagate geometry decision to docs** (LP-0MVNCMF6U006D2H7) — blocked by 5; models.ini / config.yaml comments, usage-analysis REFERENCE, log-consumer audit.
7. **Suite green and geometry assertions** (LP-0MVNCMFIF007TBFP) — blocked by 6; `/skill:test` green + slot/ctx alignment assertions.

Reuse: env plumbing already exists (`LLAMA_PARALLEL`, `LLAMA_CTX_SIZE` in start-llama.sh; `session_slot_pool_size` drives it); per-slot clamp/band logic is in `proxy/proxy/provider.py` with existing unit coverage; usage-analysis report already emits busy/prefill/decode metrics. Precedent harness: `scripts/ubatch_ab_benchmark.py`.

Pre-registered decision-gate defaults (proposal — confirm at implement time unless overridden by the producer): adopt **1 x 262K** when, relative to Arm A, (a) turns served locally does not decrease, (b) `context_too_large` + `large_context_bypass` diverts fall by >= 50 %, (c) p90 dispatch→first-byte does not worsen by > 30 %, (d) local busy % does not regress by > 10 points; otherwise keep 2 slots (or choose mode-dependent with the recorded numbers).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers (2026-10-25)

- Q: "Arm B's warm threshold: raise to the new per-slot clamp (~258K) or keep ~120K?" Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — proposed default: raise the economic ceiling ratio so warm = clamp (258,048), cold unchanged (38,000), band non-collapsed (LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP). Rationale: leaving it at 120K means the extra slot context is never routed to, defeating the arm. Final confirmation delegated to implement time unless the producer overrides.
- Q: "What makes 1 x 262K 'win'?" Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — proposed pre-registered gate above (mirrors the ubatch A/B precedent LP-0MVNBJXR6002OSPD). Confirmation delegated to implement time.
- Q: "Arm window length?" Answer: **OPEN QUESTION (producer)** — proposed default: one full night (22:00 → 06:00 local, >= 8 h), Arm A then Arm B on the same weekday type, identical length for both. Delegated to implement time.
- Q: "Write the protocol while the gate is unmet?" Answer (plan): yes — child 2 has no dependency on the busy gate (desk work), so implementation can begin immediately and the gate evidence decides when the arms may run.


## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-25Z (plan session herdr-1792903336-2608898-6919): superseded the placeholder auto-skip verdict (XS/0.00 h) with a genuine estimate (Medium effort/Medium risk); ran full /skill:plan decomposition. Created 7 children (LP-0MVNCMDK7003BWCG gate, LP-0MVNCMDW50043RSP protocol+reporter, LP-0MVNCME7Y009KC9K Arm A, LP-0MVNCMEJ6004A2QY Arm B, LP-0MVNCMEV1007R6YY comparison+decision, LP-0MVNCMF6U006D2H7 docs propagation, LP-0MVNCMFIF007TBFP suite green) in test-first order with dependency edges C3<-C1,C2 / C4<-C3 / C5<-C4 / C6<-C5 / C7<-C6. Ran the six automated review stages (trace bullets added; Key Files validated), AC coverage review proceeded (7/7), stage advanced to plan_complete. Effort/risk re-estimated (Medium, WBS from children).

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want Arm B (1 slot at 262,144 ctx) measured over a window of
identical length to Arm A, with the slot-count and context-dependent settings
adjusted consistently, so the geometry trade-off is measurable without a
threshold confound.

## Context

- Per-slot ctx is `--ctx-size / --parallel`: `--parallel 1 --ctx-size 262144` -> 262,144 per slot. `--parallel` and `session_slot_pool_size` MUST match or sessions map to nonexistent slots.
- The warm ceiling is `min(clamp, economic)` with economic = `round(local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio x local_model_ctx_size)` (0.4578 x 262,144 ~= 120,049) and clamp = 258,048 at 1 slot. Leaving the ratio unchanged keeps the warm cap at ~120K, so the extra slot context would never be routed to - the ratio/threshold must be raised so the ceiling matches the new clamp (parent AC2: "adjusted consistently").
- The cold/warm band must keep non-zero width or the cached_ratio routing check stays unreachable (LP-0MSAZXXDY005AWA1 / LP-0MSI2M5BT004BCDP).
- `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` becomes moot with one slot (prefill serialisation is inherent); record whether it is left as-is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Geometry changes are applied together and verified after restart: llama-server reports 1 slot with n_ctx 262,144, `session_slot_pool_size: 1`, warm ceiling raised to the 258,048 clamp (or an explicit recorded justification for keeping ~120K), cold threshold unchanged at 38,000. Band width and cached_ratio-check reachability are demonstrated from the routing code / unit tests, not assumed.
- AC2: Arm B is measured over a window of the same length as Arm A inside a >= 60 % busy night; raw data archived under `benchmark-results/`; reporter output recorded on this item and on the parent.
- AC3: A rollback is recorded (exact values and command to restore Arm A) and the cache-emptying restart is marked so first-byte stats are not compared across it.
- AC4: Any serving errors introduced (slot_save failed, HTTP 400/503, slot-mismatch warnings) are captured in the arm's metric table.

- Parent AC2 trace: Arm A (2 x 131K, current) and Arm B (1 x 262K) are each run for a comparable period at the gate, with llama-server --parallel / --ctx-size changed together and session_slot_pool_size plus the warm/cold thresholds adjusted consistently.

**Key Files:**
- `proxy/config.yaml` - `session_slot_pool_size`, `local_large_context_economic_ceiling_ratio`, `local_large_context_warm_cache_threshold`, `local_model_ctx_size`
- `./models.ini` - `[Qwen3]` ctx-size / parallel flags
- `./start-llama.sh` - `LLAMA_PARALLEL` / `LLAMA_CTX_SIZE` env plumbing

# Pin start-proxy.sh shell-level `--restart` preserve-vs-restart decision with a pytest test

## Problem statement

`start-proxy.sh --restart` decides whether to preserve a warm llama-server by
comparing the `config_sha256` recorded in `.llama_server_signature.json` with a
freshly computed `merged_config_sha256` of `proxy/config.yaml`; on a match it
preserves ("Preserving running llama-server (unchanged local backend config)."),
otherwise it kills and restarts llama-server. That shell branch is currently
the **only** untested consumer of the merged-config signature: the sole
coverage lives in `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh`, which
LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29 deletes (mode-era harness). The Python tests cover the hash
helper and the signature writer (`proxy/tests/test_config_merge.py`,
`proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py`), not the shell decision that acts on
them — so a regression there (e.g. comparing the wrong path, ignoring the flag)
would go unnoticed and would either kill a warm llama-server on every restart
or silently preserve a stale one.

## Users

- **Proxy operator** — the warm KV/prompt cache must survive a proxy-only
  restart, and a genuine local-backend change must restart llama-server.
- **Future implementation agents** — need the shell branch pinned so changes to
  `start-proxy.sh` restart handling fail loudly in the default suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Unchanged config preserves llama-server.** A pytest test runs a
  sandboxed copy of `start-proxy.sh --foreground --restart` whose signature
  file matches `merged_config_sha256(proxy/config.yaml, proxy/config.yaml)` and
  asserts the "Preserving running llama-server" line is emitted and the fake
  `pkill` log contains **no** `llama-server` kill.
- **AC2 — Changed config restarts llama-server.** With the sandbox config
  edited after the signature was written (merged hash changes), the preserving
  line is absent and the fake `pkill` log shows a `llama-server` kill.
- **AC3 — Fail-safe signatures.** Missing, empty or corrupt signature /
  unreadable hash → conservative restart (never an unearned preserve), asserted
  behaviourally.
- **AC4 — Explicit override still wins.** `--keep-llama-server` forces
  preservation even when the signature mismatches (flag beats hash).
- **AC5 — Sandbox isolation.** The test copies the script into a temp dir with
  stubbed `pkill`/`fuser`/`ss`/`netstat`, an isolated `$HOME`, an ephemeral port
  and a fake interpreter intercepting the final `exec uvicorn`; it never
  touches the live proxy, llama-server, TTS or ports 8000/8080/8081, and never
  issues a blanket kill. It is collected by the default pytest suite (unlike
  the bare `tests/*.sh` harnesses).
- **AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant docs entries.**
- **AC7 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- No behaviour change to `start-proxy.sh`: this is coverage for the existing
  contract. A defect found while writing it becomes a separate work item.
- Reuse the established sandbox pattern in
  `tests/test_start_proxy_launch_modes.py` (fake `python3` recording argv,
  stubbed process/port probes) rather than inventing a new harness.
- The signature schema is written by `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py`
  (`_write_llama_server_signature`: `mode`, `model`, `parallel`, `router_mode`,
  `config_sha256`); fixtures must match it.
- UK English.

## Existing state

- `tests/test_start_proxy_mode.sh` (being deleted by LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29) holds
  the only behavioural assertions for this branch; after deletion the branch has
  none.
- `grep -rln "Preserving running llama-server"` matches only that harness and
  `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh`.
- `proxy/tests/test_restart_lifecycle.py` asserts the flag is *documented*
  (`test_start_proxy_help_documents_keep_llama_server`) and pins the Python hash
  helper — not the shell preserve/restart decision.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/test_start_proxy_restart_signature.py` — new pytest test (name
  indicative).
- `tests/test_start_proxy_launch_modes.py` — sandbox pattern to reuse.
- `proxy/scripts/start-proxy.sh` — script under test (read-only).
- `proxy/proxy/config_merge.py` — `merged_config_sha256` fixture hash.
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — signature schema reference.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29** — deletes the stale mode-era harness; this item
  replaces the one piece of live coverage that deletion removes.
- **LP-0MVFJQAID007YB0H**, **LP-0MVKD0P7R002D5L8** — duplicate items closed
  in favour of LP-0MVK6JQW9003KY29 (producer decision B).
- **LP-0MUJRVYQH002IEHW** — restart signature hashes the merged config.
- **LP-0MUCEFCL6001ZXYN** — preserve-the-warm-llama-server design.

## Observed behaviour (2026-10-25, UTC)

Session `herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152` (`/skill:intake RISE-0MVLHZW7B003XEHV`) was pinned to local routing by its client (`X-Local-Preference: local-only`). The local admission guard refused it:

```
11:48:20,250  local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=prefill_budget_exceeded
              new_tokens=31246 budget_tokens=25000 free_slot=true
              priority=medium session=herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152
11:57:09,999  local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=prefill_budget_exceeded
              new_tokens=31246 budget_tokens=25000 free_slot=false  (same session)
```

Both refusals were answered with **HTTP 429 and `error: "All providers exhausted"`**:

- direct/lease path: `provider.py:10938` → `_build_exhausted_response()` → `_local_admission_reject_payload()` → `_build_local_admission_reject_response()` (`code: local_admission_reject`, `error: "All providers exhausted"`)
- contention-queue path: `provider.py:10334` / `:11291` → `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`error: "Local admission refused"`)

Remote providers were *available* throughout (`opencode-go` at 62 % effective headroom), so "All providers exhausted" is factually wrong, and the two paths disagree on the message for the same condition. The client (which retries on 429) backed off seven times and then reported the error as non-retryable; the user-visible symptom was "Error: 429 \"All providers exhausted\"".

## Goal

A local-only admission refusal is a *capacity/intent* outcome, not a chain exhaustion: it must be reported with one stable, distinguishable contract on every path, and "All providers exhausted" must be reserved for genuine chain exhaustion.

## Users

- **local-only clients** (herdr worker sessions) that must never be told the whole chain is dead when the local guard simply refused their oversized/over-budget prefill — the current prose makes them give up or retry blindly.
- **Client retry layers** that treat a truthful 429 as recoverable (`Retry-After` respects the per-reason timing from LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X) instead of terminal.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Both local-only refusal paths (direct/lease `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle` guard, contention-queue/lease `refused_local_only`) return the same shape: HTTP 429, `Retry-After` (per-reason semantics per LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X), `X-Local-Route: refused`, the `X-Local-Admission*` headers, and a body whose `error` text does **not** contain "All providers exhausted".
2. The body carries a stable `code` distinct from `all_exhausted`, `outside_time_window` and `all_slots_exhausted` — the retained value is `local_admission_reject` (Appendix Q2) — and the human-readable `detail` states that the request was pinned local-only and the local guard refused it.
3. Genuine chain exhaustion is unchanged: `code: all_exhausted` / `outside_time_window` / `all_slots_exhausted` and the existing prose remain byte-compatible for older clients.
4. `prefer-local` fallthrough behaviour is unchanged: a guard refusal with `prefer-local` still routes to the next provider and never returns the refusal response.
5. `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the refusal codes, the "local-only" semantics and the client-side action (compact/retry/allow remote).
6. Tests: unit coverage for both refusal paths asserting status, `code`, `error` text and headers; a regression test asserting a real chain exhaustion still returns the exhaustion codes; a test asserting a local-only refusal *while remotes are available* never uses the exhaustion prose.

## Constraints

- Older clients depend on the existing exhaustion `code` values and prose — AC3 is byte-compatibility for `all_exhausted`/`outside_time_window`/`all_slots_exhausted` only.
- The refusal `error` string is parsed by at least one client retry loop (the operator-reported "Error: 429 \"All providers exhausted\""); the new text must be stable and greppable.
- `X-Local-Route: refused` and `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` are already emitted by `_stamp_local_route_headers()`/`_note_local_fallback_reason()` — the fix reuses these, it does not add a parallel routing signal.
- Retry timing is owned by child LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X; this brief keeps the header contract and defers per-reason `Retry-After` values to that item.

## Existing state

- Direct/lease local-only refusal funnels through `_build_exhausted_response()` (`provider.py:5583`) → `_local_admission_reject_payload()` (`:6508`) → `_build_local_admission_reject_response()` (`:5521`), which hard-codes `error: "All providers exhausted"` and a detail claiming "no remote provider is available" — false when remotes are up.
- Queue/lease `refused_local_only` returns `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`:6310`) with `error: "Local admission refused"` — the correct prose, but a different builder with a slightly different body/headers (no `retryable`, no token headers yet).
- Both builders already return 429 + `X-Local-Route: refused` + `X-Local-Admission*` (Eta/Budget) headers + `code: local_admission_reject` (`EXHAUSTION_CODE_LOCAL_ADMISSION`, `:5518`).

## Desired change

- Direct/lease path: stop routing the local-only refusal through the exhaustion builder — return the local-only refusal response directly (same builder as the queue path) so both paths share one shape and truthful prose.
- Reserve `_build_exhausted_response()` and `error: "All providers exhausted"` for genuine chain exhaustion (unchanged codes/prose).
- Keep `prefer-local` fallthrough untouched (AC4).
- **Do not touch the prefer-local + genuine-chain-exhaustion case**: when a *prefer-local* guard refusal falls through and the remote chain is genuinely exhausted, `_build_exhausted_response()` → `_local_admission_reject_payload()` → `_build_local_admission_reject_response()` stays exactly as-is — `error: "All providers exhausted"` is truthful there and `code: local_admission_reject` is the shipped LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ AC3 contract. That builder therefore remains live; only the *local-only* branch stops routing through it.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_build_local_admission_reject_response()` (`:5521`), `_build_exhausted_response()` (`:5583`), `_local_admission_reject_payload()` (`:6508`), `_build_local_only_refusal_response()` (`:6310`), direct local-only branch (`:10938`), queue `refused_local_only` branches (`:10311`, `:11270`), `_request_local_preference()` (`:6305`), `_stamp_local_route_headers()` (`:6387`).
- `proxy/tests/test_provider_fallback.py`, `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py`, `proxy/tests/test_contention_queue.py`, `proxy/tests/test_exhaustion_error_code.py` — both-refusal-path unit coverage + chain-exhaustion regression + "remotes available" test.
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` — existing direct-path local-only test `test_local_only_refuses_429_when_guard_would_fall_back_remote` (`:416`; asserts 429, `X-Local-Route: refused`, `X-Local-Fallback-Reason`, `Retry-After`, `X-Local-Admission: reject`, `code: local_admission_reject`) — extend it with the AC1/AC6 `error`-text assertion; it does not assert the prose today, so the fix leaves it green.
- `proxy/tests/test_plan_fallback_live_e2e.py` — live-gated (`e2e_live`) chain-exhaustion regression; must keep passing for AC3 (not part of the unit scope).
- `proxy/proxy/admission_reserve.py` — `parse_preference()` (`:415`) / `stamp_route_headers()` (`:462`), the `X-Local-Preference` + `X-Local-Route` source both refusal paths rely on.
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` — `suggested_retry_after_seconds()`, shared by both refusal builders for `Retry-After`.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — `X-Local-Preference` semantics (`:1158`), `X-Local-Route` values (`:1173`), exhaustion/refusal contract; AC5 doc update lands here.

## Plan review notes (2026-10-28, plan skill)

**Decomposition decision:** no new children. This is a self-contained Small/Medium bug (expected 5.4 h, ~11 h recommended) whose six ACs are implemented directly across two code files plus docs; the tree-coverage review reports `proceed` with 0 children (6/6 ACs covered). Splitting it into per-path children would add WBS overhead to a two-file fix without isolating any risk (both paths share one builder after the change).

Review findings applied:

- **Effort/risk unknown #1 resolved** — no test asserts the direct path's exact `error` string: `test_admission_reserve.py::test_local_only_refuses_429_when_guard_would_fall_back_remote` (`:416`) asserts status, headers and `code`, never the prose. Extending it with the AC6 error-text assertion is additive; nothing needs rewriting.
- **Effort/risk unknown #2 resolved** — `_build_local_admission_reject_response()` stays live: it remains the response for a *prefer-local* refusal whose remote fallback chain is then genuinely exhausted (see "Desired change"). Only the local-only branch drops it.
- **Coverage gap found** — no test currently exercises the queue/lease `refused_local_only` branch (no `test_contention_queue.py` reference to `_build_local_only_refusal_response` or to a refusal body). AC6's queue-path unit coverage is therefore *new* tests, not an extension of an existing one; the direct path's counterpart test already exists in `test_admission_reserve.py`.
- **`X-Local-Fallback-Reason`** — already emitted by both builders (queue path from `attempt["reason"]`, direct path via `_note_local_fallback_reason()`), so it is part of the single shared shape AC1 requires even though AC1's header list does not name it. No code change; tests should assert it.
- **`Retry-After`** — both builders already compute it via `prefill_eta.suggested_retry_after_seconds()`; per-reason values stay deferred to LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X (see Constraints). This item only guarantees the header survives on both paths.
- **AC ordering for implementation (test-first)** — (1) add the queue-path refusal test + the remotes-available exhaustion-prose test (red), (2) switch the direct/lease local-only branch to `_build_local_only_refusal_response()`, (3) assert both paths agree, (4) update `routing.md`.

## Related work

- LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL — introduced `X-Local-Preference` + the AC4 refusal mechanics (completed; source of `X-Local-Route` and the `local_admission_reject` code value).
- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA admission guard (completed; source of the refusal `code`).
- LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 — cold-prefill budget enforcement (completed; `reason=prefill_budget_exceeded`).
- LP-0MU56ZM0K005F69G — stable exhaustion codes (completed; AC3's byte-compat contract).
- LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X — truthful, reason-specific retry time (discovered-from this item; `intake_complete`, blocked on U2).
- LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG — local-only enforced on every skip path (discovered-from this item; `intake_complete`).
- LP-0MVNTJQVB007QWEZ — local-only refusal invisible in proxy logs / false fallback line (open; related log-side defect).

## Risks & assumptions

- Risk: changing the refusal `error`/`detail` text breaks a client that string-matches "All providers exhausted" on the refusal path. Mitigation: prose change is the point of the bug; keep `code` stable so machine clients are unaffected (AC2/AC3).
- Risk: unifies body shape but adds fields faster than clients adopt them. Mitigation: additive body fields only; `error`/`code`/`Retry-After` stay compatible with the older shape.
- Assumption: the two refusal paths should share the queue path's builder (`_build_local_only_refusal_response`) as the single source of truth.
- Scope-creep guard: enforcement on non-admission skip paths (U2), per-reason retry timing (T8), and admission-budget tuning are separate items — not this brief's scope.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (structure — resolved): the coverage review returned `stop` because the two children do **not** decompose this bug's six ACs — they are separate defects (skip-path enforcement, retry timing). Options were: (a) detach both children, making them independent items linked via `discovered-from:` so this bug closes on its own six ACs; (b) keep them as children and treat this item as an umbrella; (c) rework the children to absorb AC1–AC3. **Recommended:** (a) — this is a self-contained bug whose ACs need direct implementation, not a delegation epic. — Answer (producer, 2026-10-26): **(a)** — detach both children. Applied: `LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG` and `LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X` now have `parentId=null` and carry `discovered-from:LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ` in their descriptions (their own `intake_complete` stage and their dep edge T8→U2 are preserved). Source: producer reply to the intake question comment.
- Q2 (code name — resolved): AC2's example `local_admission_refused` vs the shipped `local_admission_reject` (`EXHAUSTION_CODE_LOCAL_ADMISSION`, `provider.py:5518`, already used end-to-end by LP-0MVIKPCSG002B0NL and asserted in `test_admission_reserve.py:461`). Keep the existing distinct code or mint a new one? **Recommended:** keep `local_admission_reject`. — Answer (producer, 2026-10-26): **as recommended** — keep `local_admission_reject`; AC2's "e.g." wording is satisfied because it is already distinct from `all_exhausted`/`outside_time_window`/`all_slots_exhausted`. Source: `provider.py:5518`, `test_admission_reserve.py:461`.

# Local-only admission refusal is invisible in proxy logs and logs a false fallback line

## Headline

A `local-only` admission refusal returns the 429 to the client but leaves **no countable trace** in `proxy.log`, and the `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback … → routing to next provider` line is logged *before* the local-only branch returns, so the log claims routing that never happened.

## Problem statement

When the local admission guard refuses a request pinned to `X-Local-Preference: local-only`, the proxy returns the retryable 429 without ever logging the refusal itself. The only traces are the guard's own `local_admission_guard decision=reject …` line (indistinguishable from a `prefer-local` refusal that *did* fall through and succeed remotely) and a false `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback … → routing to next provider` line that states the opposite of what happened. Operators cannot count or alert on this failure class, and log-based diagnosis of these 429s mis-attributes them to chain exhaustion.

## Users

- **Proxy operator / triage agent** — must be able to attribute a client-visible 429 to "local-only admission refused" from `proxy.log` alone.
- **Monitoring analyst** — consumes log tokens for alerting/trending (`proxy-usage-analysis`, runbooks); needs a stable, countable token for this failure class.
- **`proxy-log-debug` skill / runbook readers** — grep stable log tokens documented in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

User stories:

- As a triage agent diagnosing a `429 "All providers exhausted"`-style client error, I want to grep one token and see every local-only refusal with its reason and budget evidence, so I can tell "local refused the request by design" from "the chain really ran out".
- As an operator, I want the log to never claim "routing to next provider" for a request that was refused, so fallback accounting is truthful.

## Observed behaviour (verified 2026-10-27 against `dev` HEAD)

Diagnosing session `herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152` (429 "All providers exhausted") required grepping `proxy.log` for chain-exhaustion events that never existed: the refusal leaves no refusal line at all, while a *false* fallback line is emitted for it.

```
11:48:20,250  local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=prefill_budget_exceeded
              new_tokens=31246 budget_tokens=25000 free_slot=true  session=herdr-1792897705-…
11:48:20,250  local_admission_guard_direct_fallback provider=local-qwen3 … → routing to next provider
              ← nothing was routed: the local-only branch returns the 429
```

Verified current code (`proxy/proxy/provider.py`):

- `provider.py:11014–11024` logs `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback provider=… model=… session=… reason=… free_slot=true → routing to next provider` **before** the `_preference == _PREF_LOCAL_ONLY` branch at `provider.py:11026`, which for local-only returns the 429 (`:11032`, `_build_exhausted_response`). The log states the opposite of what happened for the local-only case.
- Three return sites hand a local-only refusal to the client today:
  - contention-queue path: `provider.py:10426` → `_build_local_only_refusal_response` (429);
  - direct guard path: `provider.py:11032` → `_build_exhausted_response` (429);
  - lease path: `provider.py:11422` → `_build_local_only_refusal_response` (429).
- None of the three sites logs the refusal itself; the only common token is the guard's `local_admission_guard decision=reject …` line (`prefill_eta.py:1296`), shared with `prefer-local` refusals that fall through and succeed remotely.
- No `local_only_refusal` token exists anywhere in `proxy/`; `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the guard decision line and `X-Local-Route: refused` header but no greppable refusal token.
- Existing tests assert the misleading line *is present* (prefer-local path only, `test_local_admission_guard.py:692–697`); there are **no** tests referencing `refused_local_only` or any local-only refusal log line.

Note: the original description's line numbers (direct `:10432`/`:10450`, contention `:10785`) are stale — the code moved; the behaviour they describe is unchanged and still present.

## Goal

Every local-only admission refusal is attributable from the proxy log alone, and no log line claims routing that did not happen.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback … → routing to next provider` line is emitted only on an actual fall-through to the next provider. For a local-only refusal it is either not emitted or clearly qualified — never with "→ routing to next provider" wording.
2. Each local-only refusal emits exactly one INFO line with stable `key=value` fields, e.g.
   `local_only_refusal session=… provider=… reason=… new_tokens=… budget_tokens=… eta_prefill_seconds=… budget_seconds=… priority=… route=refused`,
   on **every** refusal path (contention-queue `provider.py:10426`, direct guard `provider.py:11032`, lease `provider.py:11422`). The budget/ETA/token values must come from the admission decision actually used at that site (carried on the decision object logged at `prefill_eta.py:1296`); `session`, `provider` and `priority` come from the dispatch context — the same values that decision line logs. The existing guard `local_admission_guard decision=…` line remains unchanged (shared with `prefer-local`), so refusals are counted by `local_only_refusal`, not by `decision=reject`.
3. The refusal is countable from the log by a single stable token — `local_only_refusal` — and `proxy/docs/routing.md` (Observability section) documents the token so runbooks and the `proxy-log-debug` skill can grep it.
4. Tests:
   - a test asserting the `local_only_refusal` log line is emitted for a local-only refusal on each path (contention-queue, direct guard, lease);
   - a test asserting the misleading "→ routing to next provider" line is **not** emitted for a refused local-only request on the direct path;
   - a test asserting a `prefer-local` fall-through still emits the existing `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback … → routing to next provider` line (regression guard for `test_local_admission_guard.py:692`).
5. Verification note: the 2026-10-25 11:57:09 case (guard rejection of `herdr-1792897705-4039879-16152`) is reproducible in a test, and the resulting log output is shown in the work item.

## Constraints

- No change to the 429 response contract (body/headers) — response-text consistency is the sibling item **LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ**, pending there.
- No change to `prefer-local` fall-through behaviour.
- No change to the guard's own `local_admission_guard decision=…` line (stable tokens at `prefill_eta.py:1296`).
- Logging must never break routing: refusals log from inside the already-returned branch (best-effort, in the pattern of `_note_local_fallback_reason`).

## Assumptions (documented)

- "Exactly one INFO line" (AC2) means exactly one `local_only_refusal` line per refused request; the guard's `decision=reject` line and any `Fallback triggered` lines for genuine fall-throughs are unchanged and not counted as refusal lines.
- Quality of the line is what matters for counting: the token must be greppable and stable; field names mirror the guard decision's existing keys (`new_tokens`, `budget_tokens`, `eta_prefill_seconds`, `budget_seconds`, `projected_wait_seconds` where available).
- Updating the `proxy-log-debug` skill (`.pi/skills/…`) is out of scope (repo-boundary rule); documenting the token in `proxy/docs/routing.md` satisfies AC3 and the skill can be updated as a follow-up work item.

## Risks

- **Merge/behavioural overlap with sibling `LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ`** — both touch the direct-guard return block (`provider.py:11026–11032`). Sequence the two items (or implement together) to avoid conflicting edits; this item only moves/quotes the log line, it does not change the response. If `LP-0MVNTJJGX00375VQ` lands first and switches the direct path to `_build_local_only_refusal_response`, AC2's site list still holds (the log line goes at the same branch).
- **Scope creep risk** — logging-related opportunities (e.g. request-header logging for `X-Local-Preference`, `proxy-log-debug` skill update) are recorded below as related work/out of scope, not added to this item.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — the three refusal return sites (`:10426`, `:11032`, `:11422`) and the misleading log (`:11014–11024`); add the `local_only_refusal` INFO line just inside each local-only refusal branch, and move/qualify the fallback log.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — Observability section (`~:1051`) documents the decision line; add the `local_only_refusal` token.
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — extend for direct-path refusal and prefer-local regression (`:692–697`); add direct-path non-emission test.
- `proxy/tests/test_admission_reserve.py` — existing local-only refusal coverage to extend: `test_local_only_refuses_429_when_guard_would_fall_back_remote` (`:416`) and the prefer-local regression `test_prefer_local_still_falls_back_remote_when_refused` (`:466`) assert only the response/headers today, not the log line.
- `proxy/tests/…` — coverage for the remaining refusal paths (no local-only log test exists for the lease path; the cq/lease harnesses already used by `test_hard_routing_cap.py`/`test_prefill_eta.py` can be reused).
