## Summary

Measure whether the child-port discovery fix (LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF, deployed
2026-10-26T21:01Z) actually eliminates router-responder `GET /slots ... 500`
responses over a full 24 h production window, and record the raw counts as
auditable evidence.

**Earliest run: 2026-10-27T12:00Z.** Window:
**2026-10-27T12:00Z → 2026-10-28T12:00Z.** If the fix (or a follow-up restart)
lands later than that, shift the window to start 24 h after the last relevant
deployment and record the new timestamps in a comment.

**Window state verified at planning (2026-10-28T04:40Z):** the window is
**still open** (≈7 h 20 m remaining at verification time). Production facts:
proxy pid **3791954** started **2026-10-27T10:16:11Z** and is still running
(18 h 23 m uptime) — the fixed proxy has been up continuously since **before**
the window opened, and **no proxy restart has occurred inside the window**, so
the AC6 restart condition is satisfiable. No pre-window baseline comment was
recorded at 12:00Z; see "Baseline reconstruction" under the execute-time plan
for why the counter delta is nonetheless provable.

## Problem statement

Router-proxied `GET /slots` polls returned HTTP 500 at ~9 % during giant
prefills because child-port discovery silently failed and every proxy poll
traversed the router. The fix replaced discovery with a rotation-proof signal
and routed every call site through it, but the only proof that matters is a
production 24 h window with zero such 500s — the pre-fix evidence (1,754
router 500s in the 2026-10-26 log) is not proof of absence.

## Users

- **Producer / maintainer** — "As the operator, I want a dated, reproducible
  measurement of router-responder `/slots` 500s so I can close the residual-500
  bug and trust the fix, instead of re-reading raw logs myself."
- **On-call agent (herdr downtime worker)** — "As an unattended agent, I want a
  deterministic method and explicit verdict rule so my pass/fail report does
  not depend on my own judgement of ambiguous counts."
- **Downstream users** — chat/agent clients that see 500s and 5–7 s slot-poll
  latency when slot queries serialise behind a busy child.

## Acceptance Criteria

Refined at intake per producer decisions Q1(a), Q2(b), Q3(a):

- **AC1** — **Chat-model path: zero.** The windowed count of router-responder
  `GET /slots ... 500` responses attributable to the chat model is **0**.
  Responder split: lines with no `[pid]` prefix are the router, `[pid]`-prefixed
  lines are the model children; per-file counts are reported for every
  `llama-server*.log` file whose mtime falls inside the window (Q1a).
- **AC2** — **Raw router and child counts reported**, so a silent switch back to
  router polling cannot masquerade as a pass: router-responder `GET /slots`
  200 / 400 / 500 and model-child 200 / 400 / 500 counts for each file in the
  window. `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` output is attached verbatim.
- **AC3** — **`slots_stale` share reported** for `status_request` polls in the
  window: the primary figure is *all* `status_request` polls (directly
  comparable to the pre-fix baseline **579/899** in the 2026-10-26 file), with
  the active-prefill subset (`active_query=true` or `local_active_query=true`)
  reported as a secondary figure (Q3a).
- **AC4** — **Fallback evidence reported, split by path** (Q2b):
  `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  delta across the window plus the (throttled, undercounting)
  `slots_child_port_unavailable` warning lines, attributed by model.
  - Chat-model (`Qwen3`) fallbacks: **any occurrence fails the check.**
  - Embed-model (`mxbai-embed`) fallbacks: reported separately as a
    **non-blocking observation**; if any occur, a new bug item is filed at
    window end, linked `discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`.
- **AC5** — **Reproducibility:** the exact commands/regexes (or script
  invocations) used, the window start/end timestamps, the pre-window baseline
  snapshot (counter values, log line count, proxy pid + start time) and the raw
  counts are all recorded as a work-item comment.
- **AC6** — **Restart integrity:** any proxy restart inside the window is
  detected (pid change) and reported; if one occurred, the counter delta is
  declared unavailable and the verdict relies on per-file log counts with the
  limitation stated explicitly.
- **AC7** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC8** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Method (agreed: Q1 option (a) — hybrid)

Measured with existing tooling plus two log families:

```bash
# 1. Window-start snapshot (also record: date -u, pid start time, log line count)
date -u; ps -o lstart= -p "$(pgrep -f 'uvicorn proxy.server:app')"
wc -l < /var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log
curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep 'llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total'

# 2. Window-end snapshot (same commands, 24 h later) -> counter delta = exact
#    windowed fallbacks when the proxy was not restarted in between.

# 3. Responder/status split per file (reuses the triage CLI: no timestamps in
#    llama-server logs, so scope by the files whose mtime falls in the window)
python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy --llama-file 'llama-server.log' --summary

# 4. Fallback warnings (throttled to one line per interval -> undercounts;
#    the counter above is authoritative)
grep -c 'slots_child_port_unavailable' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log

# slots_stale share (existing baseline method)
grep -o 'slots_stale=[a-z]*' /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log | sort | uniq -c
```

Take a **pre-window baseline snapshot** immediately before
2026-10-27T12:00Z (counter values + `llama-server.log` line count + proxy pid
start time) so the window delta is unambiguous.

> **Status: not done.** No snapshot comment exists for 2026-10-27T12:00Z. The
execution plan below reconstructs the baseline from monotonic-counter
evolution plus pid `lstart`, and states the limitation explicitly (AC5).

## Execution plan (exact recipe — run at/after 2026-10-28T12:00Z)

Steps 0–2 must be re-verified at run time, not trusted from this block; they
are read-only and cheap. Steps 3–6 produce the evidence; step 7 records it.

### Step 0 — window gate

Do **not** measure before **2026-10-28T12:00Z**. An earlier run measures a
partial window and is not acceptable as the AC evidence.

### Step 1 — restart integrity (AC6)

```bash
date -u
ps -o pid,lstart,etime -p "$(pgrep -f 'uvicorn proxy.server:app' | head -1)"
```

Expected: a single pid **3791954** with `lstart` **2026-10-27T10:16:11Z** ⇒ no
restart inside the window. Any other pid/`lstart` ⇒ record the restart time,
declare the counter delta unavailable, and fall back to per-file log counts
with the limitation stated (AC6).

### Step 2 — fallback counter (AC4, exact)

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/metrics | grep 'llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total'
```

A Prometheus counter that has never been incremented emits **no sample line**
(only `# HELP` / `# TYPE`). That is the state observed at planning — quote the
raw output verbatim, because "absent sample" is the auditable form of "0".
Range-vector deltas are not needed: a monotonic counter reading 0 on a process
that started before the window ⇒ windowed delta = 0.

### Baseline reconstruction (AC5, replaces the missed 12:00Z snapshot)

State the limitation explicitly and rebuild the baseline from: proxy pid +
`lstart` (step 1); the counter's never-incremented state (step 2); the per-file
line counts read at window end. The proof is monotonicity, not a start sample:
the process started 1 h 44 m before the window opened and its counter is still
0.

### Step 3 — llama-server file set (AC1 / AC2)

```bash
ls -l --time-style=full-iso /var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server*.log*
```

Window set (mtime inside 2026-10-27T12:00Z → 2026-10-28T12:00Z):
`llama-server.log-2026-10-28` (logrotate `copytruncate` copy at 00:00Z; content
= 2026-10-27T00:00Z → 2026-10-28T00:00Z) and the live `llama-server.log`
(content = 2026-10-28T00:00Z → window end). `llama-server.log-2026-10-27.gz`
has mtime 2026-10-27T00:00Z ⇒ outside the window, exclude it.

llama-server access lines carry **no timestamps**, so this union covers
2026-10-27T00:00Z → window end: a **superset** of the window, carrying 12 h of
extra pre-window traffic. Consequence: **zero router-responder 500s across the
superset proves zero inside the window** (report the over-count direction); a
non-zero count needs the per-file split plus the caveat that the window
boundary is approximate at ±12 h granularity.

```bash
python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
  --llama-file 'llama-server.log-2026-10-28' --summary
python3 scripts/slots_500_triage.py --log-dir /var/log/llama-proxy \
  --llama-file 'llama-server.log' --summary
```

Record both per-file outputs verbatim (AC2) and sum the responder/status matrix
(router 200/400/500, child 200/400/500).

### Step 4 — proxy.log file set (AC3, plus AC4 warnings)

`proxy.log` is timestamped and self-rotates every 6 h, and the daily
`copytruncate` copy (`proxy.log-YYYY-MM-DD_HH`) can duplicate a range — so
**file names do not reliably delimit the window**. Derive each candidate's own
first/last timestamp from its lines, keep the parts intersecting the window,
and dedupe overlapping ranges (keep one generation per timestamp range):

```bash
for f in /var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*; do
  case "$f" in *.gz) zcat "$f";; *) cat "$f";; esac \
    | awk -v f="$f" 'NR==1{first=$0} {last=$0} END{print f"	"substr(first,1,19)"	"substr(last,1,19)}'
done
```

At planning time the window-relevant generations were
`proxy.log.2026-10-27_10`, `proxy.log.2026-10-27_16`, `proxy.log.2026-10-27_22`,
`proxy.log-2026-10-28_00` and the live `proxy.log` — indicative only; re-derive
the set from timestamps at run time.

```bash
# AC3 primary: all status_request polls in the window (comparable to 579/899)
grep -h 'status_request' <window files> | grep -o 'slots_stale=[a-z]*' | sort | uniq -c
# AC3 secondary: active-prefill subset
grep -h 'status_request' <window files> \
  | grep -o 'active_query=[a-z]*\|local_active_query=[a-z]*' | sort | uniq -c
# AC4 warnings, per file (throttled -> undercounts; the step-2 counter is authoritative)
for f in <window files>; do printf '%s	' "$f"; grep -c 'slots_child_port_unavailable' "$f"; done
grep -h 'slots_child_port_unavailable' <window files>   # attribute each by model=
```

### Step 5 — verdict rule

**GREEN** ⇔ chat-model router-responder `/slots` 500s = 0 **and** chat-model
fallback delta = 0 (counter **and** warning lines). Embed-model
(`mxbai-embed`) occurrences are reported separately and file a linked bug
(`discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`) without ever making the verdict RED.
Any other positive chat-model count ⇒ **RED**: name the model/responder and
file the linked bug. Report router/child 200/400 counts and the `slots_stale`
share alongside either way (AC2/AC3).

### Step 6 — evidence comment (AC5)

One comment recording: window start/end; `date -u` at run time; pid + `lstart`
+ uptime; the raw `/metrics` line(s); both per-file triage outputs verbatim;
the `proxy.log` file set with each file's observed first/last timestamp; the
dedupe/overlap rule applied; the counts; the `slots_stale` primary and
active-prefill figures; the "llama-server lines are timestamp-free ⇒ ±12 h
boundary approximation" caveat; the missed-baseline limitation; the verdict;
and any linked bug id.

AC7 and AC8 are code-change boilerplate on a measurement item — see the OPEN
QUESTION in the Appendix for the interpretation used.

## Existing state (evidence gathered at intake, 2026-10-26T23:36Z)

- **Fix is deployed.** Proxy pid 3482545 restarted 2026-10-26T21:01:42Z
  (after fix commits `f58e8964` 2026-10-26T12:51Z and `189864fc`
  2026-10-26T13:00Z, both on `dev`). Blocking item LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF is
  `completed`/`in_review`. _(Superseded 2026-10-27T10:16:11Z: pid 3482545 was
  replaced by pid **3791954**, still running at planning time. Both fix commits
  are ancestors of `dev`. The restart predates the window, so the window is
  restart-free.)_
- **Early signal the chat path is fixed.** Live 90 s spot check at
  23:36Z: 78 model-responder `/slots` events, **0** router-responder `/slots`
  events, 0 HTTP 500s.
- **Residual fallbacks exist post-fix.** `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  is already **4** since the 21:01:42Z restart, and one throttled
  `slots_child_port_unavailable` WARNING was logged at **21:01:46Z** for
  `model=mxbai-embed` (the embedding child). The current `llama-server.log`
  also still holds ~4 router-responder `/slots` lines in its last ~25 min.
  Consequence: AC4's "one occurrence fails" will very likely trip on
  restart/embed transients — resolved as Q2 option (b).
- **Rotation breaks the single-file method.** `llama-server.log` is rotated
  in-process (`rotate_llama_logs(keep=15)`, numeric `llama-server.N.log`) and
  by the `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy` safety net (daily, `copytruncate`,
  `dateext` → `llama-server.log-YYYY-MM-DD`). `proxy.log` self-rotates every
  6 h (`proxy.log.YYYY-MM-DD_HH`). A 24 h window therefore spans several
  files, and llama-server access lines carry **no timestamps**
  (`scripts/slots_500_triage.py` documents this: "no timestamps in
  llama-server logs; the corpus is per-file"). A single-file grep cannot
  cover the window — resolved at intake as Q1 option (a), hybrid.
- **Cumulative figures today** (`--llama-file 'llama-server.log'`, whole
  file, spans more than one day and predates the fixed restart):
  router 200 = 38,369; router 400 = 452; router 500 = 2,753; model 200 /
  child 200 = 68,610 + 8. Non-zero router 200s show that **direct LAN clients
  poll the router** legitimately, so raw router counts are not pure
  proxy-fallback evidence.
- **`slots_stale` alive in the current `proxy.log`**: 2,019 false / 1,952 true
  (49 % true) since the current file began — usable as an intermediate
  reference, not the window figure.
- **No existing windowed tool.** `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` classifies by
  responder/status and supports `--llama-file <glob>`, but has no
  `--since/--until`; window scoping is a manual file-set decision.

## Desired change

No product code change: this item is a **measurement and evidence** task. Its
"change" is a recorded, reproducible verdict (counts, commands, window
timestamps, and either a green pass or a new linked bug when red).

**Verdict rule (agreed):** GREEN = windowed chat-model router-responder
`/slots` 500s are 0 **and** the chat-model fallback delta is 0, with router and
child 200/400 counts and the `slots_stale` share reported alongside. RED = any
positive chat-model count; a RED verdict must name the model/responder and
create a linked bug item (`discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`). Embed-model
fallbacks never make the verdict RED — they raise a linked bug instead.

## Constraints

- Window must be a full 24 h with the fixed proxy running; restarts inside the
  window must be detected and reported (they reset counters).
- No production restart, no config change, and no code change is needed for the
  measurement itself (`start-proxy` must not be invoked unless the proxy dies).
- llama-server logs are timestamp-free → any time attribution is per-file and
  approximate; this limitation must be stated in the recorded comment, never
  silently smoothed over.
- If the verdict is red, a new bug item is created (linked
  `discovered-from:LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF`); LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF is never silently
  reopened.
- Measurement must not perturb the proxy: read-only log greps plus a single
  `/metrics` scrape at start and end.
- **Execution gate (recorded at planning, 2026-10-28T04:40Z):** the window
  closes at **2026-10-28T12:00Z**; a run started earlier measures a partial
  window and must not be used as the AC evidence. Assignee `Map` is the
  scheduling hold — clear it at/after 2026-10-28T12:00Z to release the item.

## Key Files

- `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` — existing responder/status classifier; needs a windowed (file-set) invocation or a documented file-selection recipe.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_discover_local_child_port`, `_resolve_local_slots_target`, `_warn_child_port_fallback` (emits `slots_child_port_unavailable`; throttled).
- `proxy/proxy/metrics.py` — `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` counter (exact, reset on restart).
- `proxy/proxy/lifecycle.py` — `rotate_llama_logs(keep=15)` in-process numeric rotation (file boundaries = restarts).
- `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy` — daily `copytruncate`/`dateext` safety net for both log families.
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/llama-server.log` (+ `llama-server.N.log`, `llama-server.log-YYYY-MM-DD`) — router vs child `/slots` access lines.
- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log` (+ `proxy.log.YYYY-MM-DD_HH`) — `slots_stale`, `status_request`, `slots_child_port_unavailable`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (high): verdict goes red on embed-model transients.** Post-fix
  counter already 4 with one `mxbai-embed` warning in ~2.5 h of uptime; a
  literal AC4 makes the window almost certainly red for a cause that is not
  the busy-child 500 storm. **Resolved (Q2b):** embed fallbacks are reported
  separately and never make the verdict RED; a linked bug is filed instead.
- **Risk (medium): coverage gap.** If a rotation/restart lands mid-window, the
  single-file greps under-report. **Resolved (Q1a):** counter delta plus
  file-set aggregation, restart-aware (AC6).
- **Risk (medium): attribution.** Direct LAN clients polling the router
  produce router 200/400/500s that are not proxy-fallback symptoms; without
  source attribution the check can be red for unrelated noise. **Mitigation
  (agreed):** the fallback counter is the primary chat-path signal; raw router
  counts are reported for masquerade detection only, with the limitation
  stated in the recorded comment.
- **Risk (low): timing slip.** The 12:00Z window needs an agent at both ends;
  a late start truncates the window. Mitigation: snapshot first, then wait.
- **Assumption:** "the fix is deployed" means proxy pid started after
  `189864fc`; re-verify pid start time at window start rather than trusting
  this brief.
- **Scope-creep guard:** a reusable windowed measurement script (e.g.
  `--since/--until` on `slots_500_triage.py`) is a **separate follow-up item**,
  not part of this measurement.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVP7525P008RXMF** — Residual router-proxied `/slots` 500s: audit
  remaining call sites and enforce direct child-port polling (completed; the
  fix under test here).
- **LP-0MVP7HV7Q001AJF8** — Router `/slots` HTTP 400s: `?model=` resolution
  path (86 residual router 400 responses) — sibling split, shares AC2's 400
  reporting.
- **LP-0MTCMEV1G0022A35** — `/slots` 500-storm triage tooling
  (`scripts/slots_500_triage.py`), reused here.
- **LP-0MTIHZ8M5005ZAU8** — earlier (inert) direct-child fix; historical
  context for why the rotation-proof signal was needed.
- **LP-0MTDGBRPU003Z7KU** — 5–7 s router-proxied slot-poll latency measurement
  (the latency symptom of the same defect).
- Automated find-related report: work items LP-0MQYEY34L000H3O8 (ui.py
  `_extract_router_model_ids` NameError), LP-0MRB2ABNX008SF9P (proxy logger
  output), LP-0MQ6EGGJ6002JHZX (single-model mode) — same log/proxy surface,
  no AC overlap.

## Interview decisions (resolved)

- **Q1 = (a) Hybrid window scoping.** Fallback-counter delta from `/metrics` at
  window start/end (exact, restart-aware) + `scripts/slots_500_triage.py`
  counts summed across every `llama-server*.log` file whose mtime falls in the
  window, reported per-file with the "llama-server lines are timestamp-free →
  approximate attribution" caveat. No code change; a `--since/--until` upgrade
  to the triage CLI stays a separate follow-up item.
- **Q2 = (b) Chat-model zero tolerance, embed reported separately.** `Qwen3`
  path: zero router-responder 500s and zero fallbacks. `mxbai-embed` fallbacks
  are a non-blocking observation and spawn a linked bug at window end if any
  occur.
- **Q3 = (a) All `status_request` polls as the primary `slots_stale`
  denominator**, with the active-prefill subset as a secondary figure.

Source: producer reply "As recommended" (2026-10-27T00:48Z, accepting the three
recommended options in comment LP-C0MVPWPEKW004SSKP).

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-28T04:40Z — planning session (Map).** Effort/risk pre-check
  returned `skip` (Extra Small / Low), so the item was reviewed rather than
  decomposed; no child items were created (single measurement slice, one
  vertical pass through evidence → verdict → record). Changes made: verified
  window state block added to the Summary; "Execution plan" added with the
  exact commands, file-set derivation and dedupe rule; the missed 12:00Z
  baseline snapshot documented with the monotonic-counter reconstruction (AC5)
  and the superset-bound argument (AC1/AC2); the 2026-10-28T12:00Z execution
  gate added to Constraints; the superseded intake pid annotated in "Existing
  state"; one non-blocking OPEN QUESTION added for AC7/AC8. Six review stages
  run; AC coverage review returned `proceed` (leaf item, no children).
  Effort/risk reused from intake (Extra Small / Low, score 2/25) — no scope
  change to re-estimate.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION (plan, 2026-10-28T04:40Z)** — AC7 ("all related
  documentation updated … README, wiki or docs site entries") and AC8 ("full
  project test suite must pass with the new changes") read as code-change
  boilerplate, while "Desired change" states explicitly that this item makes
  **no product code change**. Working assumption used by the plan (does not
  block execution): AC7 is satisfied by the recorded measurement evidence (plus
  any doc touched if the verdict spawns a follow-up) and AC8 is satisfied by
  the standard full-suite gate (`/skill:test`) on any change this item
  produces — which is none. Directed to: producer. Why it matters: if a doc
  note (e.g. a measured-results entry under `docs/`) or an actual suite run is
  intended as part of this item's evidence, the execution plan needs one more
  step. Not blocking: the measurement and verdict are unaffected.

- Q1 "How should the window be scoped across rotated logs?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-10-27T00:48Z): option (a), hybrid** — counter delta + per-file
  triage counts across the window's file set, caveat documented. Source:
  interactive reply "As recommended" (comment LP-C0MVPWPEKW004SSKP). Research: `llama-server.log`
  has no timestamps; in-process numeric rotation (`rotate_llama_logs`,
  keep=15) and logrotate `copytruncate`/`dateext` mean a 24 h window spans
  several files; `scripts/slots_500_triage.py` supports `--llama-file` globs
  but no time window; `proxy.log` is timestamped and its
  `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` counter is exact but resets on
  restart.
- Q2 "How strict is the zero-tolerance rule?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-10-27T00:48Z): option (b)** — chat-model zero tolerance; embed-model
  fallbacks reported separately as non-blocking with a linked bug if present.
  Source: interactive reply "As recommended". Research:
  post-restart counter = 4 fallbacks
  (`no_child_port_router_mode`), 1 throttled `slots_child_port_unavailable`
  WARNING at 2026-10-26T21:01:46Z for `model=mxbai-embed`; 8
  `proxying request to model mxbai-embed` lines exist in the current log, so
  embed discovery signal is sparse rather than absent.
- Q3 "What exactly is the AC3 `slots_stale` denominator?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-10-27T00:48Z): option (a)** — all `status_request` polls as
  primary, active-prefill subset secondary. Source: interactive reply "As
  recommended".
  Research: parent intake recorded the pre-fix baseline as 579/899 *all*
  `status_request` polls in the 2026-10-26 file; `status_request` lines expose

data.description:
# Intake Brief — In-request local re-dispatch after a prefill-deadline cancellation re-arms the lease and holds the gate ~6 min

## Problem statement

A local dispatch cancelled by `prefill_deadline_exceeded` (120 s) does not reliably
end the session's claim on the local gate: the same session immediately re-dispatches
local and acquires a **fresh dispatch lease**, whose record stays `active` without
producing a first byte and is released only by the no-progress watchdog ~308 s later.
Other sessions are denied (`local_dispatch_denied`, `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue
reason=local_lease_active`) for 311–322 s each — beyond the epic's <=5 min per-hold bound
(LP-0MVKN9IRP003XJH6 AC1) and the only remaining `wedge_denials > 0` signal
(`ac1.wedge_denials: 3` in the 2026-10-25 21:19 → 2026-10-26 21:19 window, verified
`ac1.verdict_met: false`).

## Users / stakeholders

- **Operator** (user story): *"As an operator, I want a local dispatch cancelled by the
  prefill deadline to stop holding the local dispatch gate, so the next session is not
  denied for longer than the epic's <=5 min bound."*
- **Sessions sharing the local gateway**: during the hold they are forced remote
  (3 refusals in this incident, 311–322 s each; the 2026-10-23 incident was ~3 orders
  of magnitude larger and unbounded).

## Mechanism decision (intake determination, 2026-10-26 — log `proxy.log.2026-10-26_131429`)

**Candidate (a) is confirmed; candidate (b) is refuted as the operative mechanism:**

1. `[local] POST` fires **147–150 ms after** each `lease_released reason=prefill_deadline`
   (10:39:36,396 → 10:39:36,546; 10:41:36,629 → 10:41:36,776) — a fresh local dispatch
   in the same request/retry window, so a *new* record is acquired **after** the release.
2. `_extend_lease_during_prefill` only mutates an **existing active** record, yet
   `lease_extended_during_prefill ... in_flight=True` resumes at 10:41:46, exactly 10 s
   after the 10:41:36 release — proving a fresh **active** record exists post-release
   (mechanism (b) — release removing a differently-keyed record — would leave no record
   for the extension path to touch; the release path only logs `lease_released` when it
   actually removed a record).
3. The hold chain: record acquired ~10:44:25 (same session re-acquisition — always
   permitted by `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`): no extensions after 10:44:18, denials at
   10:46:57/10:47:08 with `owner=01a177c6…`, released 10:47:33 by
   `reason=no_progress_watchdog` (≈10:44:25 + 180 s watchdog + 10 s sweep) ≈ **308 s
   unproductive hold** → AC3's 300 s bound fails.
4. **Residual gap (OPEN at implementation time):** the thrash cooldown was armed for this
   session at 10:39:36 and re-armed at 10:41:36 (`prefill_thrash_cooldown_started cooldown_s=600`),
   yet **zero** `routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` lines appear for
   `01a177c6-…` in the whole file across 4 successive local dispatches (10:39:36 → 10:44:25),
   while `herdr-…` sessions are consistently skipped. The
   `_prefill_thrash_cooldown_remaining(_session_id, …)` gate in `provider.py` returned 0 for
   this session despite the armed key. Either the arm key differs from the check key
   (session-identity mismatch between router.py's arm and provider.py's check), or a
   dispatch path bypasses the local-branch gate — the AC1 deterministic test must pin this
   before choosing the fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A dispatch cancelled by `prefill_deadline_exceeded` is **not re-dispatched locally
   within the same request** (the detour goes to the next provider), **or** the
   re-dispatch is refused while the session's prefill-thrash cooldown is active — and the
   gate actually engages: asserted by a deterministic test with an injected clock and a
   stubbed local dispatcher (mirroring `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py`) that
   would have caught this incident (i.e. it fails on the pre-fix behaviour of a fresh
   lease acquired 150 ms after the release). The test must also isolate why the
   2026-10-26 gate did not engage (arm-key vs check-key or bypass path) and assert the
   engaged skip.
2. After the cancellation the session's lease **and** `local_prefill_in_flight` marker are
   cleared before any retry, and the cancelled upstream prefill is cancelled (or proven
   dead) so `_extend_prefill_lease` cannot re-extend from a stale marker.
3. Any hold that does remain is bounded by <=300 s (the epic's 5 min bound): a regression
   test asserts release within 300 s simulated (no-progress watchdog must bound the record
   even when the session re-acquires).
4. `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py --measure` over a >=24 h post-fix window
   reports `ac1.wedge_denials: 0` with no 300 s+ unproductive hold chain and
   `ac1.verdict_met: true`.
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (code comments,
   `proxy/docs/routing.md`, `proxy/README.md`, and the prefill-recovery verification
   doc/README as applicable).
6. The full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The prefill deadline (120 s / 90 s default) is a deliberate
  "detour, don't kill" backstop; the fix must not push first-byte latency above
  `local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds` and must not disable the thrash cooldown
  (`local_prefill_thrash_cooldown_seconds`, rollback knob 0).
- The no-progress watchdog (180 s) and 10 s cleanup sweep cadence are production-bounded
  self-healing; the <=300 s bound must hold without weakening them.
- No-preemption lease semantics (same-session re-acquisition permitted) are load-bearing for
  legitimate long prefills; the fix must not break admission for genuine in-flight prefills.
- Fix scope lives in this item (the epic closes with this residual tracked; see Related work).

## Existing state

- `router.py`: on `prefill_deadline_exceeded` it arms the 600 s thrash cooldown, releases
  the lease + marker (`_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`), then the chain falls through —
  but the *next* local attempt (same request re-dispatch/retry) acquires a fresh lease;
  the thrash gate in `provider.py` did not engage for the affected session (see mechanism
  decision §4).
- `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` counts `active or expires_at > now` records as occupied;
  the sweep only deletes `not active AND expired` records outright, and the active-expired
  category extends records whose llama-server slot still reports processing — a wedged
  record can hold the pool until the no-progress watchdog.

## Desired change

- The post-deadline detour must be **terminal for local within that request** (no in-request
  local re-dispatch), and/or the thrash-cooldown gate must demonstrably engage for every
  local dispatch attempt (close the arm-key/check-key or bypass-path gap).
- Every local dispatch record must be released (or bounded) within <=300 s of its last
  progress, regardless of which path acquired it (deadline detour, same-session
  re-acquisition, active-expired sweep).
- `local_prefill_in_flight` must never outlive the dispatch it marks (no stale marker
  re-extension).

## Risks, assumptions and failure modes

- **Assumption:** the deployed llama-server's first byte genuinely arrives with the SSE
  headers (the monitor's premise), so a 120 s deadline miss means no client-visible byte —
  supported by 0 `Stream started: provider=local` lines for the session in the window.
- **Risk — over-correction:** making the deadline detour terminal for local could deny
  local to a session whose next *legitimate* request would have prefilled warm; mitigated by
  the existing 600 s cooldown already having this intent, and by clearing the cooldown on a
  successful local first byte.
- **Risk — masking the gate gap:** capping renewals only (the LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0 shape)
  bounds the hold but leaves the un-engaged thrash gate; AC1 must assert the gate engages.
- **Failure mode to test:** stale `local_prefill_in_flight` marker re-extending a record
  whose upstream is dead (`in_flight=True` extensions resumed after the release).
- **Scope-creep risk:** lease fairness (LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0) and the 115 s second-slot
  residual (LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I) overlap this evidence; record any such work as linked
  items, do not absorb it here.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — local re-dispatch / slot-retry path after a deadline
  cancellation; thrash-cooldown routing gate (`_prefill_thrash_cooldown_remaining`),
  `_dispatch_local` call sites
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — deadline arm/release sequence
  (`prefill_deadline_exceeded`, `_record_prefill_thrash_cooldown`,
  `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`), `_try_acquire_local_dispatch` caller
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — `_extend_lease_during_prefill`,
  `_release_prefill_deadline_dispatch`, `_try_acquire_local_dispatch`,
  `_cleanup_stale_local_dispatch`, `_watchdog_no_progress`,
  `_prefill_thrash_cooldown_*`, `_dispatch_lease_key`
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_thrash_wedge.py` — deterministic injected-clock/stub harness
  to extend for the re-dispatch assertion
- `scripts/prefill_recovery_verification.py` — AC4 measurement (`ac1.wedge_denials`,
  hold-chain accounting in `measure_wedge_denials`)

## Related work

- **LP-0MVKN9IRP003XJH6** — epic "Wedged prefill lease loop holds the local dispatch gate
  ~4 h" (completed/in_review); epic AC1 is the <=5 min bound this item enforces. The
  producer removed the epic's `depends-on` edge so the epic can advance: the epic closes
  with this residual tracked here (blocking edges on this item: none).
- **LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0** — Lease fairness (cap consecutive prefill-lease renewals); same
  log evidence; producer decided the epic closes with this residual tracked here, and the
  fix *may* land there instead only if the cooldown/lease cap also covers the in-request
  re-dispatch (AC1 allows either mechanism; otherwise fix here and note the overlap).
- **LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I** — 115 s/24 h second-slot residual (separate admission-shape
  residual; not to be conflated).
- **LP-0MU498TWH008DBCI** — Contention queue ignores prefill-saturated dispatches
  (completed; related queue behaviour).
- **LP-0MRB29PP60012UYF** — Stale local dispatch lease blocks subsequent requests
  (completed; prior stale-lease fix lineage).
- **LP-0MVLGNUDJ009NRX2** — AC3 re-judgement that surfaced this residual
  (24 h window 2026-10-25 21:19 → 2026-10-26 21:19).

## Appendix: clarifying questions and answers

- Q (producer, via description): "Which mechanism holds the gate — (a) the same request's
  local re-dispatch acquiring a fresh record, or (b) a differently-keyed release?"
  — Answer (intake, from log `proxy.log.2026-10-26_131429` + code read): **(a)** confirmed;
  (b) refuted (see Mechanism decision). Source: `[local] POST` 147–150 ms after each
  `lease_released`; `lease_extended_during_prefill in_flight=True` resuming 10 s after the
  release proves a fresh active record (the extension path only mutates an existing active
  record); watchdog release at 10:47:33 = 10:44:25 acquisition + 180 s + 10 s sweep.
- Q (implement comment): "the release line carries `endpoint=http://localhost:8080`, the
  extension path passes its own endpoint argument — is endpoint-key normalisation the
  defect?" — Answer (intake): no. `_dispatch_lease_key` does **not** normalise
  (`localhost:8080` vs `192.168.0.199:8000` are distinct keys), but the 10:41:46 post-release
  extension proves a live record under the extension path's key, and the release path only
  logs `lease_released` when it removed a record — so the record that wedged was acquired
  after the release, not left behind by a wrong-key release. The endpoint mismatch on the
  release line remains worth a defensive check (key-form consistency) at implementation time.
- Q (OPEN QUESTION — implementation must answer before choosing the fix): why did the
  600 s thrash cooldown armed at 10:39:36/10:41:36 for `01a177c6-…` fail to produce a
  single `routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` across 4 successive local
  dispatches (10:39:36 → 10:44:25), while `herdr-…` sessions were consistently skipped?
  — Answer: **_not yet determined_**. Hypotheses to test with the AC1 injected-clock harness:
  (i) session-id mismatch between router.py's arm key (`session.session_id`) and
  provider.py's check key (`_session_id`, raw `x-session-id`/`session_id` header); or
  (ii) a local dispatch path that bypasses provider.py's local-branch gate.
  **Recommended (advisory):** treat the gate engagement as load-bearing — assert it in the
  deterministic test and fix whichever arm/check or bypass gap the test surfaces, rather
  than only capping renewals (LP-0MVOJ6KAW004EBV0-style), so AC1 holds for any path.
  Idempotence note: re-running intake must not duplicate this appendix entry.

## Goal

When the local entry is unavailable for a non-admission reason (cooldown, lease held, `context_too_large`, contention-queue expiry), derive the retry hint from the real expiry — not from the ETA formula.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the local entry is unavailable for a non-admission reason (cooldown, lease held, `context_too_large`, contention-queue expiry), the retry hint is derived from the real expiry (`_compute_retry_after` / cooldown remaining / lease remaining), not from the ETA formula.
2. Cooldown-driven refusal: `Retry-After` = cooldown remainder, sourced from real cooldown state (`unavailable_providers` / `_usage_reset_at`).
3. Lease-held refusal: `Retry-After` = lease remaining (`_get_lease_timeout_seconds`).
4. Contention-queue expiry: `Retry-After` = queue expiry time.
5. `context_too_large`: treated as not time-retryable (like `prefill_budget_exceeded` — no `Retry-After`, `retryable: false`, guidance in `suggested_action`).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — refusal builders, `_compute_retry_after()` (:4261), `_stamp_local_route_headers()` (:6387), `_usage_reset_at` / `unavailable_providers` cooldown state
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` — lease state (`_dispatch_lease_key`, `_get_lease_timeout_seconds`)
- `proxy/proxy/contention_queue.py` — contention-queue expiry data

## Dependencies

**BLOCKED on** LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG (local-only enforcement on all skip paths). This AC requires that cooldown skips refuse rather than fall through to remote, which is the scope of that item.

## Related work

Covers AC3 of LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X.

## Goal

Stop `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=prefill_deadline` events: local dispatches that are **admitted, then released before producing a first byte** by the 120 s prefill deadline. Each event wastes the accepted prompt's prefill (~5,586 tokens measured) and detours the request to a remote provider after a 120 s stall.

## Measured evidence (2026-10-26 09:06:07 → 2026-10-27 09:06:07)

Source: `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`, 44 files, 79,058 lines. 116 `prefill_deadline_exceeded` WARNINGs; **114 carry the enriched `local_eviction_after_acceptance` snapshot**.

| Metric | P10 | P50 | P90 | Max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `estimated_tokens` (prompt) | 2,478 | 35,008 | 66,958 | 86,022 |
| `new_tokens` (priced compute) | 150 | 2,384 | 14,302 | 46,538 |
| `eta_prefill_s` (admission prediction) | 4.8 | 34.1 | 91.7 | 200.2 |
| `elapsed_s` (dispatch → cancel) | 120.1 | 120.1 | 133.8 | 136.0 |

Findings:

1. **Not an over-budget-token problem.** Only 2 of 114 exceeded `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` (25,000). Median `new_tokens` = 2,384. Median actual/predicted ratio = **3.52×**.
2. **Not second-slot head-of-line blocking** (contradicting the LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I hypothesis): 68% of events overlapped **nothing** (no other prefill, no decode, no other cancelled prefill); `local_in_flight_requests` reached 2 in only 11% of windows.
3. **29 events (25%) are "fake-warm".** Prompt ~56k, `new_tokens` 17–182 (implied `cached_ratio` 0.997–0.999), ETA 3.7–13.8 s, cancelled at 120 s.
4. **The requests were prefilling, not idle.** 648,008 wasted prefill tokens / 116 events = 5,586 tokens over 120 s = **46.6 tok/s**, matching the measured prompt-eval p10 (43.1 tok/s). llama.cpp computed ~5,600 tokens, not the 17–182 the proxy priced.
5. **Root cause: warmth is predicted, never measured at admission.** All 5,456 `routing_resident_prefix` decisions in the window carry `n_past_actual=none` (0 measured). `resolve_resident_prefix` returns `reuse_ratio=1.0` for `RESIDENCY_SOURCE_SESSION_SLOT`, and `Check 4` then sets `reusable = estimated_tokens`, so an unmeasured slot owner always passes `estimated_tokens - reusable <= cold_cache_threshold` and is **admitted regardless of prompt size**.
6. **89 of 114 events (78%) are repeats** across 33 `(session, prompt)` clusters and only 43 distinct sessions — the retry loop was the amplifier. **Fixed by LP-0MVQITN6P008DPLB** (committed to dev as `1911e2ec`), leaving ~25 first-occurrence events that are the residual target of this item.

## Design decision (2026-10-27, producer-approved — Option D)

The original ACs (Option A: prompt-size floor making unmeasured owners fall through to conservative pricing) were measured (implement run comment LP-C0MVQIWP8B009O9OI) and code-verified (plan comment LP-C0MVQJ7I1H0093NK4) to be **unsafe and ineffective**: 252 working local prefills ≥ 20k tokens sit in the same 18k–78k band as the doomed events (177 with first byte < 10 s), no admission-time predicate can separate warm owners from clobbered ones (`n_past_actual=none` everywhere), and `Check 5` re-pricing still admits (measured ratio 0.999). The producer approved **Option D — early abort on *measured* prefill progress**:

- **No admission-ladder change**: `Check 4`/`Check 5` and `resolve_resident_prefix` stay byte-for-byte identical, so the working warm path (252 large, 70% first byte < 10 s) is untouched.
- **Measure during dispatch, not admission**: llama.cpp b8782 (build `e97492369`) does **not** expose `n_past` on `/slots` (verified live: fields absent), but its chat-completions parser copies unknown request keys, so the proxy can inject `return_progress: true` upstream and receive `prompt_progress` events inside the existing SSE stream — **zero llama.cpp change** (verified in `tools/server/server-common.cpp` `oaicompat_chat_params_parse` → `params_from_json_cmpl` L265; events emitted at `server-context.cpp` ~L1450-1467).
- **The deciding signal**: the first `prompt_progress` event carries `{total, cache, processed, time_ms}` where `cache = n_prompt_tokens_cache` = the **actual reused prefix** (set at `server-context.cpp` L2455 before the initial 0% progress event). A warm dispatch shows `cache ≈ 0.999 × total`; a fake-warm one shows `cache` tiny against a large `total` — the re-prefill is visible immediately, at a few hundred tokens of waste.
- **Abort**: when measured actual new tokens (`total − cache`) exceed the admission-priced compute by a configurable bound, release the lease early (before the 120 s deadline), log `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=measured_cache_deficit`, and detour to remote — wasting seconds, not 120 s.

## Scope

**In:** proxy-side injection of `return_progress` on local streaming dispatches; parsing `prompt_progress` from the reframed SSE stream; an early-abort decision against admission-time pricing; a config knob (0/disabled = pre-change behaviour) with docs; fail-open on missing/malformed progress; observability for the new eviction reason so the post-deploy window can quantify waste reduction.

**Out:** any change to `Check 4`/`Check 5`/`resolve_resident_prefix`; changing the ETA regression, the deadline value, or the cold-prefill token budget; llama.cpp changes of any kind; `n_past` restoration on `/slots` (upstream, tracked separately).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Measured reuse drives the decision.** The proxy parses `prompt_progress.{total,cache,processed,time_ms}` from the local streaming response (unit-tested with real b8782 event shapes).
- **AC2 — Early abort on measured deficit.** A dispatch whose first progress event shows `total − cache` far above the admission-priced new tokens (fake-warm signature: large prompt, tiny `cache`) is released early with `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=measured_cache_deficit`, detouring to remote in seconds rather than 120 s. Unit test with a synthetic progress stream.
- **AC3 — Warm path byte-for-byte unchanged.** A genuinely warm dispatch (`cache ≈ 0.999 × total`) never trips the abort; all admission-ladder decisions (`session_slot`/`measured`/`non_resident`) and the first-byte path are identical to today. Regression tests for both.
- **AC4 — Rollback knob.** A documented config key disables the capture+abort (`0`/disabled = pre-change behaviour), and a test proves the rollback path reproduces the exact old behaviour (no `return_progress`, no early release, full 120 s deadline).
- **AC5 — Fails open on error.** Any exception in capture/parse/decision or missing progress events resolves to today's behaviour (no early release, no hard local outage). Test asserts this.
- **AC6 — Observability.** The new eviction reason is attributable in the usage report (distinct from `prefill_deadline`) so the post-deploy window can count it and measure wasted-token reduction.
- **AC7 — Existing suite green.** Changed-scope tests pass in the implement gate; the full suite is enforced at the dev push.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/router.py` (`proxy_to_local` → upstream body injection + SSE reframing loop where `prompt_progress` is parsed)
- `proxy/config.yaml` (`server` keys for the measured-cache abort knob and its documentation block)
- `proxy/tests/` (SSE progress capture tests, abort-decision unit tests, warm-path regression tests)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/log_parser.py` (attribution of the new eviction reason — the parser is reason-generic, `RE_EVICTION_REASON`, so no allow-list change was needed)
- `proxy/proxy/prompt_progress.py` (b8782 `prompt_progress` event contract + capture helpers — F1/F2, delivered `2f263d90`/`1590e879`)
- `proxy/proxy/measured_prefill.py` (per-dispatch measured-prefill state and reuse ratio — F2, delivered `1590e879`)
- `proxy/proxy/measured_cache_abort.py` (pure measured-cache-deficit abort decision — F3/F4, delivered `87f238a2`/`1908f431`)
- `docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md` (capture contract, invariants, rollback, replay and post-deploy measurement procedure)

## Assumptions

- "Measured" means the `cache` value from llama-server's `prompt_progress`, which is ground truth for the actual KV-cache reuse at dispatch time — not a prediction.
- `return_progress` survives the chat-completions parser by the verified unknown-key copy loop; the spike in the implement phase must confirm the full path on the live build (a native-`/completion` fallback exists if the field is dropped, at proxy-only cost).
- The abort bound defaults to a value that cannot trip a genuinely warm dispatch (warm `cache/total` ≥ 0.99) while catching the fake-warm signature (measured ratio often < 0.01); operator-tunable.
- Streaming local dispatches are the primary target; non-streaming requests keep today's deadline behaviour unless the stream-loop change makes progress capture trivial for them too.

## Rollback

Set the new config key(s) to disabled (`0`/`false`). No code change, no restart-ordering constraint beyond the usual process restart.

## Delivery state (plan re-run 2026-10-28)

Ten of eleven children are `completed`/`in_review`; the Option D implementation is on `dev`
(F1 `2f263d90`, F2 `1590e879`, F3 `87f238a2`, F4 `1908f431`, F5 `25854928`, AC1 `d0ddc7ba`,
AC2 `1500db96`, AC6 `48ac1fb7`).

`LP-0MVS03KCV005BTGE` (post-deploy ≥ 24 h measurement) stays **deliberately parked at
`open`/`idea`**: it is time-gated on a `/skill:start-proxy --restart` onto the F4 build plus
≥ 24 h of live traffic. Its plan content is complete (goal, scope, four measurable ACs,
earliest-run gate, exact measurement commands in
`docs/dev/measured-prefill-capture.md#post-deploy-measurement-parent-ac4ac5`). It is *not*
advanced to `plan_complete` because a schedulable stage re-exposes it to the 2026-10-28
false-completion incident, where an implement run auto-`finish`ed the never-worked item and
briefly advanced this epic to `in_review`. Un-park it only once the post-F4 restart has
happened.

Plan: changelog — 2026-10-28 (plan skill re-run)
- Key Files completed with the four artifacts the implementation actually created
  (`prompt_progress.py`, `measured_prefill.py`, `measured_cache_abort.py`,
  `measured-prefill-capture.md`); `log_parser.py` note corrected to "reason-generic, no
  change needed".
- AC coverage re-verified: 7/7 parent ACs mapped to children (100%), no gaps.
- Dependency graph re-verified: test items precede implementation items for all delivered
  children; the parked child's F5 prerequisite is recorded in prose only (not wired as a
  `wl dep` edge, since F5 is complete and the child is parked).
- No child work items created, closed or re-scoped: none of the six review stages found a
  gap that was both clearly needed and unambiguous.

# Tune idle-admit eligibility to prefill feasibility (measured 0/31 conversion)

Discovered from: LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB (lease-gate decision item) — the AC5
tuning follow-up for LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD.

## Goal (user story)

As the operator, I want the idle-admission override (`server.local_idle_admit_enabled`)
to admit only requests the local backend can prefill to first byte inside
`local_prefill_deadline_seconds` / the ETA-guard queue budget, so the override
no longer spends GPU time on doomed prefills with zero served responses.

## Measured evidence (window 2026-10-22 21:48:05 → 2026-10-23 21:48:05)

31 `routing_idle_admit` events, **0 conversions** (0/31 local first bytes):

- 22 dispatched to a local slot and cancelled at `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
  (90 s deadline in force at the time; `lease_extended_during_prefill ...
  progress=None alive=False in_flight=True` → no observable prefill progress
  before the deadline), then detoured remote.
- 9 rejected on arrival by the ETA admission guard
  (`local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct`,
  projected prefill 63–362 s vs the 60 s contention-queue budget).
- 0 refused by the `local_lease_active` gate; 0 first bytes.

Admitted prompt sizes 39–119 K cold tokens; window-wide `prefill_deadline_exceeded`
totalled 482 (= ~90 s per slot per abort). The after window was ~2× busier than
the before window (large_context_bypass 1,790 → 3,702; remote fallbacks 6,953 →
12,888), so this is a heavy-load measurement; the mechanism (admit → ETA-refuse
or deadline-abort) is load-independent.

Machine artifact: `docs/dev/idle-window-measurement-2026-10-22-to-2026-10-23.json`.

## Scope (candidate mechanisms to evaluate with the evidence)

- Prompt-size / projected-prefill eligibility **at admit time**: refuse the
  idle admit (keep the economic remote fallback) when `evaluate_admission`
  prices projected prefill beyond the deadline or the ETA guard would reject —
  i.e. make the override's admitted verdict consistent with the guard's
  (LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 AC3c already consults the guard; measure whether the
  dispatched-and-cancelled residue remains because the guard's calibrated
  refusal and the deadline disagree).
- Priority gating: only admit below a `high`-priority tier if interactive
  latency risk is unacceptable.
- Only if the 0-conversion persists after eligibility: reconsider the
  prefill-aware idle clock (option 5 of LP-0MVK16GME007EYUW) — the measured
  window had **zero** silent-prefill refusals, so this is the fallback, not
  the primary fix.
- Explicitly NOT in scope: preempting foreign dispatch leases — rejected in
  LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB (option 1 decision); do not reopen without new evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The override's admit decision is priced against projected prefill
   feasibility (ETA-guard budget + prefill deadline) and the measured
   0/31-conversion outcome is used as the regression signal: after the change,
   an equivalent window must show idle-admitted dispatches either converting
   to a first byte or being refused **before** dispatch (no
   `prefill_deadline_exceeded` on an idle-admitted session).
2. The fix is fail-safe: it can only refuse admissions the current code
   admits — it can never admit a request the guard or deadline refuses today.
3. Any new knob is config-read at dispatch time / hot-reloadable
   (`POST /admin/reload-config`), default preserves today's behaviour until
   the tuning demonstrates improvement (LP-0MVDT94F0003VHUA AC4).
4. Unit tests cover: admit-eligibility refusal on projected prefill beyond
   the deadline; the unchanged `context_too_large` cap; a calibrated vs
   uncalibrated (fail-open) bucket; and that the lease gate is untouched.
5. Docs: `docs/dev/idle-window-measurements.md`, `proxy/config.yaml` knob
   comments and `proxy/README.md` updated; decision on the flag recorded on
   LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF (window outcome was `measure`/`tune`, not
   `enable_by_default`).

## Related work

- LP-0MVK35UX20081BIB — parent decision (option 1: lease gate unchanged).
- LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD — parent measurement (window AC1–AC4 of record).
- LP-0MVNBJYE3003MF6J — ETA-guard and prefill-deadline interaction review
  (budget/deadline re-derivation).
- LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I — residual deadline evictions with zero prefill progress.
- LP-0MVN4LBZ500281Z7 / LP-0MVKUKEU80022C3U — guard/deadline bounds the
  override already consults.

## Goal

Test-first proof for parent AC4/AC5: every line that decides "not local" names the
parsed preference, and `priority_routing` can be tied to a session/request without
correlation heuristics.

Parent: LP-0MVNU2KTK009D4AG.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `caplog` assertions cover, for each of the three preference values: `routing_skip_local`, `routing_check`, `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`, `local_admission_guard_direct_fallback`, the chain-resolution `Skipping provider=<local> … in cooldown` line, and the quota hard-stop skip line — each carries `preference=<parsed value>`.
- `priority_routing` (both dispatch cycles) carries session attribution (`session=` and/or `request_id=`) alongside the existing `model=`, `priority=`, `providers=`, `preference=` fields.
- Additive-only assertion: a helper parses `key=value` pairs from each line and asserts all pre-existing keys are still present (guards log-grep tooling).
- A request with no header logs `preference=prefer-local` (never an empty/absent value).
- Red-before-green evidence recorded in a comment on this item.

Parent-AC traceability (each line quotes the parent criterion this child discharges):

- Covers parent AC4: Every skip/fallback line that decides "not local" logs the parsed preference (`preference=local-only|prefer-local|remote-ok`) so an intent violation is visible in `proxy.log`; `priority_routing` keeps its existing fields (additive change only).
- Covers parent AC5: Attribution is possible: the `priority_routing …` line (or its successor) carries the session id / request id, so a preference can be tied to a specific request without correlation heuristics.
- Covers parent AC6: Tests: one test per skip reason asserting local-only ⇒ refusal and prefer-local ⇒ remote dispatch (table-driven); a regression test asserting `remote-ok` still strips local; a test asserting the preference appears on the skip/fallback log line.

# Goal

Stop abandoned local dispatches from leaving llama-server busy and from
throttling local routing for 10 minutes afterwards, so `capacity_hint` can be
trusted as "saturated only with live work" and the herdr downtime dispatcher
stops being starved by the cooldown.

## Context (measured, LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV; published by LP-0MVOG7IX6006MZ23)

Post-fix night 2026-10-24 20:00 → 2026-10-25 07:00:

- 332 local dispatches were abandoned in the window: `prefill_deadline` 260,
  `session_evicted` 60, `no_progress_watchdog` 11, `client_disconnect` 1
  (`measurement.json` → `abandonment_events`).
- llama-server kept finishing the abandoned jobs, so later **fresh** `/slots`
  polls reported slots `is_processing` with no proxy-side dispatch record: 247
  status polls (2.12 %) read `capacity_hint=saturated` with
  `local_in_flight_requests=0` and `slots_detail_stale=false`. Every poll is
  attributed to an abandonment within 600 s (`prefill_deadline` 204,
  `session_evicted` 43, unattributed 0) in
  `saturated_without_live_work_attribution.csv`.
- Each `prefill_deadline` breach starts a 600 s `prefill_thrash_cooldown`, and
  `routing_skip_local reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` fired 916 times in the
  window — the leading candidate explanation for the night reaching 5 herdr
  downtime dispatches instead of the ≥ 10 target.

Evidence: `~/proxy-usage-reports/2026-10-24_post-fix-night-measurement/`.
This is NOT a capacity-signal defect: the reconciliation rules held (zero
stale-detail poll claimed `saturated` without live work).

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A local dispatch abandoned by `prefill_deadline` / `session_evicted` /
  `no_progress_watchdog` is actively cancelled upstream (llama-server
  cancellation/abort), or its continued work is otherwise excluded from the
  capacity signal, so `saturated` with `local_in_flight_requests=0` and fresh
  detail is not produced for abandoned work.
- AC2: The 600 s `prefill_thrash_cooldown` is re-evaluated: a cooldown started
  by an abandonment must not skip local routing for a subsequent window where
  the GPU is demonstrably free (measure `routing_skip_local
  reason=prefill_thrash_cooldown` before/after).
- AC3: Tests cover the new cancellation/cooldown behaviour with mocked
  llama-server responses (no live dependency) and the full suite passes.
- AC4: A re-measurement over one comparable night (same tool, same window
  length) reports (a) `saturated`-without-live-work ≈ 0 and (b) herdr downtime
  dispatches within the parent's ≥ 10/night target, or documents why not.

## Constraints

- Do not weaken the truthful-status rules from LP-0MVKSXR4P001V0CM: a fresh
  snapshot that genuinely reports processing must still be able to say
  `saturated`.
- Re-measurement is read-only evidence collection; never restart or kill the
  proxy to obtain it.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/handlers.py` (prefill deadline / lease release path)
- `proxy/proxy/router.py`, `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` (dispatch
  cancellation, cooldown)
- `scripts/capacity_signal_verification.py` (re-measurement)

## Definition of Done

ACs met, tests green, nightly re-measurement recorded with artifacts.

## Goal

Produce the measured evidence the AC3 closure verdict needs: a ≥24 h post-landing window of `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=prefill_deadline` events, with the user-traffic / audit-session split and a per-event cause attribution (occupancy / capacity / predicted-warmth), so the tracking item LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I can decide AC3(a) versus AC3(b).

## Background — the original premise is superseded by later measurement

- The scheduler epic LP-0MVN1IQTF0037WTG and its occupancy-aware child LP-0MVOFVCA2008DQVE are **completed** (commit `8b7ab7a2`, in `HEAD`; the proxy restarted with it at 2026-10-26T10:23Z).
- A later measurement on LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (window 2026-10-26 09:06 → 2026-10-27 09:06, 114 events) **falsified the second-slot head-of-line hypothesis**: 68 % of events overlapped no other prefill or decode, and `local_in_flight_requests` reached 2 in only 11 % of windows. 29 events (25 %) were "fake-warm": prompt ≈56 k, priced `new_tokens` 17–182, `eta_prefill_s` 3.7–13.8 s, cancelled at 120 s.
- The cause attributed there is predicted-but-unmeasured warmth: all 5 456 `routing_resident_prefix` decisions in that window carry `n_past_actual=none`. The fix is LP-0MVQIT9QY007QU27 (Option D, `measured_cache_deficit` early abort), whose F5 LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD owns the fix's own ≥24 h post-deploy measurement.
- **Do not repeat F5.** Consume its output where available and add only what the AC3 verdict needs (user/audit split, occupancy-vs-warmth attribution, per-reason counts).

## Scope

**In:** window and deploy-timestamp selection; log mining over `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*`; user-traffic vs audit classification using the **same classifier** as the parent AC4 measurement (LP-0MVN3KMGI009BZ0D); per-event attribution; a recorded dataset plus the exact commands needed to reproduce it.

**Out:** any code change (admission, deadlines, budgets, queue bounds, slot counts); the AC3 verdict itself (sibling verdict item); rewriting parent AC4. Any further admission-maths change discovered while measuring is filed as a new linked work item (`discovered-from` this item), never folded in here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Window and deploy timestamps recorded.** The ≥24 h measurement window and the deploy timestamp of every admission-affecting change inside it (at minimum `8b7ab7a2` and the Option D commit) are recorded on this item **before** measuring; any proxy restart, config reload or slot-count change inside the window is recorded as a re-base event.
- **AC2 — Parent-AC1 evidence reported.** The 22-event/7.4 h measurement (12 user-traffic) with the `progress=0` signature and the audit-load split is reported against the new window using the same classifier, so the two reports are comparable and can be referenced from the parent AC4 comment by the verdict item.
- **AC3 — Parent-AC3 counts reported.** For the window: total `reason=prefill_deadline` events, the user-traffic vs audit-session split, the hourly rate for each, and the `new_tokens` / `eta_prefill_s` / `elapsed_s` distributions — reported against both the 22-event/7.4 h baseline and the 114-event fix-item window.
- **AC4 — Cause attribution per event.** Each event is classified as **occupancy** (another session's prefill or lease in flight in the same slot pool), **capacity** (slot saturation with no other occupant) or **predicted-warmth** (large prompt, tiny priced `new_tokens`, actual prefill progress far above the priced compute), with the classification rules and evidence columns recorded. The occupancy share is the direct test of this item's original hypothesis.
- **AC5 — Conversion accounted.** `reason=measured_cache_deficit` (Option D) is reported alongside `prefill_deadline`, so a fall in one reason is never misread as the residual disappearing.
- **AC6 — Parent AC3 mapping (evidence half).** "**AC3 — Closure.** Closed only when either (a) the scheduler epic lands and a post-landing window shows zero user-traffic `prefill_deadline` evictions after acceptance, or (b) the producer explicitly re-scopes parent AC4 with an agreed threshold and the re-scoped criterion is met." — this item supplies the measured evidence for path (a) and, when (a) fails, the evidence for the (b) re-scope proposal; it does not close the tracking item.

- `/var/log/llama-proxy/proxy.log*` (window evidence)
- `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/analyze_proxy_usage.py` (existing analysis flow)
- `proxy/proxy/admission_events.py` (`log_local_eviction`, `EVICTION_REASONS` — the closed reason vocabulary)

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — the post-fix window is a valid evidence window.** It is only valid if the deploy timestamps are recorded first and no admission-affecting change or slot-count change occurs inside it (AC1 re-bases the window otherwise).
- **Risk — attribution drift.** The user-traffic / audit classifier must be the parent AC4 one, or the two reports stop being comparable (AC2).
- **Risk — misreading the reason conversion.** A fall in `reason=prefill_deadline` with a rise in `reason=measured_cache_deficit` is Option D doing its job, not the residual disappearing (AC5).
- **Reuse:** LP-0MVR7IXAI002QXXD (F5) already measures the fix's own post-deploy window; this item consumes that output rather than duplicating it.

## Deliverables

A recorded window analysis (dataset + reproducible commands) posted as a comment on this item, with the attribution table and explicit pointers for the AC3(a) / AC3(b) verdict.

## Problem

In the free-slot (direct-dispatch) admission-refusal branch of `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`_prefill_admission_guard(... reason_label="eta_exceeds_budget_direct", free_slot=True)`), the recorded refusal reason collapses every non-deadline decision reason to `eta_exceeds_budget_direct`:

```python
if str(_direct_admission.reason).startswith("prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline"):
    _direct_reason = "prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline"
else:
    _direct_reason = "eta_exceeds_budget_direct"
```

So on the free-slot path:

- `prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget` is labelled `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` (mis-attributed cause).
- `prefill_budget_exceeded` (a prompt permanently over the flat cold-prefill cap) is labelled `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` — a **time-retryable** ETA reason. The refusal then advertises a `Retry-After` for a prompt that waiting cannot fix, i.e. the 2026-10-25 retry-storm defect (LP-0MVNTT4X8009IO2X AC1) is still reachable whenever a local slot happens to be free.

Observed while writing LP-0MVQ23A6S007DVDM: the queue path preserves the decision reason verbatim (`_maybe_queue_for_local_slot` returns `_admission.reason`), the direct path does not — so the two paths answer the same reason with different retry semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The direct-path refusal records the governing decision reason verbatim (`prefill_eta_exceeds_deadline`, `prefill_eta_exceeds_safety_budget`, `prefill_budget_exceeded`, `eta_exceeds_budget`), keeping `eta_exceeds_budget_direct` only as the dispatch-path log label.
2. A free-slot request whose prompt exceeds `local_cold_prefill_budget_tokens` gets the `prefill_budget_exceeded` refusal contract (no `Retry-After`, `retryable: false`, token evidence) — driven end-to-end through `proxy_with_fallback` with a free slot.
3. Tests: table-driven direct-path coverage of each reason, asserting `X-Local-Fallback-Reason` / body `reason` match the governing decision reason.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — direct free-slot guard refusal branch, `_direct_reason` mapping
- `proxy/tests/test_local_admission_guard.py` — direct-path reason tests
- `proxy/tests/test_cold_prefill_budget.py` — cold-cap refusal contract

Producer-directed re-measurement of the capacity signal and herdr downtime
dispatch recovery on the **current** build, because the 2026-10-24 night cycle
was ruled not representative of work being dispatched ("run the measures again
in another 12 hours").

## Why this rerun exists

The first post-fix window (`LP-0MVOG7IP80003MLV`: 2026-10-24 20:00 → 2026-10-25
07:00) measured a build **without** the `/slots` child-port resolver
(`f58e8964`, landed 2026-10-26 12:51 UTC): every proxy `/slots` query traversed

throttled by 600 s `prefill_thrash_cooldown` after prefill-deadline breaches).

`f58e8964`, and (b) covers a period with normal dispatch activity, so the
stale-rate and dispatch-recovery questions can finally be judged.

## Goal (user story)

As the operator of the LLM proxy, I want local prefills observed while the other slot is busy to be calibrated as their own rate distribution and used to price contended admissions, so that the guard stops admitting dispatches at a rate the GPU cannot deliver under co-residency (measured 2-4x optimistic).

## Context

Parent evidence (2026-10-28): the guard priced a 6,659-token prompt at `eta_prefill_s=13.9` (~479 t/s) while the llama-server prompt-eval median for the same day is ~120 t/s (p25 85 / p75 202 / max 763, n=229). The calibration window mixes solitary and contended dispatches, so the fitted rate is dominated by uncontended runs. Prefill is serialised (`local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1`) but prefill+decode batching is not: an occupant that is *generating* halves the newcomer's prefill throughput. Co-residency is therefore a real conditioning variable, not noise.

## Scope

- Tag each calibration sample with co-residency and store contended samples in a separate `(model, bucket, contended)` window.
- Co-residency evidence: (a) the admission-time `busy_slots` snapshot already stamped on the request/dispatch record, OR'd with (b) a live check at first-byte time that another session's live dispatch record is active for the same endpoint. Either signal marks the sample contended.
- Price contended admissions from the contended window when it holds `>= local_admission_guard_min_samples` samples; otherwise fall back to the solitary window and say so in the log (fail-open — never a guessed multiplier).
- Expose the chosen bucket on the decision log and on `/llama/local/status`.
- Warm-prompt pricing is untouched: `cached_ratio` / coded-token path unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `record_dispatch_sample` accepts a co-residency flag and stores the sample in a distinct contended window; a unit test seeds both windows and asserts each sample lands in the right one (including the OR of admission-time and first-byte-time signals).
- AC2: `coefficients()` / `estimate_prefill_seconds()` accept a contended selector; a contended admission (`busy_slots >= 1`) is priced from the contended window when it is calibrated and falls back to the solitary window when it is not — both paths unit tested.
- AC3: The `local_admission_guard` decision log carries `rate_bucket=contended|solitary|solitary_fallback` and `contended_samples=<n>`; a test asserts the field for a contended decision, a solitary decision and the uncalibrated-contended fallback.
- AC4: With a contended window seeded at the measured median (~120 t/s, ~8.3 ms per new token), a cache-cold 6,659-token prompt prices `>= 55 s` (parent AC2) instead of the recorded 13.9 s optimistic figure.
- AC5: Warm-prompt admissions are unaffected: a prompt with `cached_ratio >= 0.9` prices identically to before the change (test compares against the pre-change computation).
- AC6: Full test suite green; the existing prefill-ETA, deadline, occupancy and budget tests keep their intent (any assertion updated only because the log line gained fields is called out in the commit message).

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router.py` (first-byte sample recording)
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` (`_stamp_local_admission_evidence` co-residency stamp)
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` (`_dispatch_evidence`)
- `proxy/tests/test_prefill_eta_contended.py` (new)

## Notes

- Do **not** change `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` (60) or `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (120); the 60 < 120 < 840 < 900 ordering must stay intact (parent scope guardrail).
- Rollback: existing `local_admission_guard_policy: observe|off` remains the documented escape hatch.

## Goal (user story)

As the operator of the LLM proxy, I want the contended-pricing semantics, the occupant-remaining rebase and their rollback paths documented in the same places the guard is documented today, so a future operator can reason about the guard without re-deriving the calibration.

## Scope

- `proxy/config.yaml` comment block: document contended vs solitary calibration, `rate_bucket` values, and any new keys, next to the existing `local_admission_guard_*` entries. Guardrail values (60/120) untouched.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` and `docs/llama-router.md` (where they document the admission guard): a "Co-residency calibration" note with the two changes from parent LP-0MVS8T6F4006DGG3 and the documented rollback (`local_admission_guard_policy: observe|off`).
- Module docstring of `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py`: add a "Contended (co-resident) calibration" section referencing LP-0MVS8T6F4006DGG3 and the `rate_bucket` decision-log field.
- Cross-reference the parent item and its children in the docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `proxy/config.yaml` documents the contended bucket, the `rate_bucket`/`contended_samples` decision-log fields and the fallback-to-solitary behaviour; `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` and `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` values are unchanged.
- AC2: `proxy/docs/routing.md` (and `docs/llama-router.md` where present) explains the contended rate selection and the occupant-remaining rebase with the ordering guardrail note (60 < 120 < 840 < 900).
- AC3: `docs/` contains a "Plan: changelog"-style cross-reference block listing the parent item and the children implementing the fix — prose only, no `.worklog/` writes from this item.
- AC4: No behaviour change: this item is docs-only; a docstring/comment spelling fix does not count as a behaviour change.

## Key Files

- `proxy/config.yaml`
- `proxy/docs/routing.md`
- `docs/llama-router.md`
- `proxy/proxy/prefill_eta.py` (docstring)

## Dependencies

- Requires the contended rate bucket and occupant-remaining rebase to be implemented so the docs describe the shipped behaviour.

data.description:
# tree_coverage AC extraction truncates hard-wrapped bullets (false coverage "stop")

Discovered from: LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD — while planning that item, the shared
AC-coverage review reported every parent AC as uncovered with `recommendation:
"stop"`, even though the children (LP-0MVJXGSEG0045IAF, LP-0MVRCLPVI0057116)
clearly cover the scope.

## Root cause

`extract_acceptance_criteria()` in `skills/shared/tree_coverage.py` treats each
physical line as one AC. The project's descriptions hard-wrap AC bullets at
~80 columns, so a single bullet like "A ≥24 h post-deploy window is analysed
with `proxy-usage-analysis` and reports, next to the baselines above: ..." is
cut to its first fragment ("...and reports,"). Similarity matching against
child ACs (also wrapped) then scores 0.05–0.18, below the 0.2 auto-close
floor, and every AC is reported uncovered (coverage 0 %, recommendation
"stop"). Re-flowing the AC text into single lines restores full sentences but
the matcher still cannot see the mapping because both sides are truncated.

## Impact

- False `stop` results block stage advancement on wrapped items (LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD
  sat `intake_complete` while its measurement work was already recorded).
- Coverage % is meaningless (0 %) for well-maintained wrapped descriptions.
- Auditors/planners must manually re-verify coverage on every wrapped item.

## Acceptance criteria

- `extract_acceptance_criteria()` joins wrapped continuation lines of a bullet
  into a single AC entry instead of truncating at the first line (indented
  sub-list markers still excluded as before).
- A regression test covers a hard-wrapped multi-line AC bullet and asserts one
  complete AC is returned.
- Re-running coverage review on LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD after the fix no longer
  reports all 5 parent ACs as uncovered (score movement is what matters, not
  a specific threshold).

## Key Files

- `skills/shared/tree_coverage.py` (agent infrastructure — do not edit without
  operator approval; the fix itself is a separate authorised change)
- `skills/plan/tests/`
